sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an Extended Essay (EE) tutor in Mumbai to the writing phase
paragraphs: A request for IB DP Extended Essay home tuition in Mumbai produces a shortlist of two or three tutors from the subject group the essay is registered in, not a general writing coach. We ask four things before we shortlist anybody: the registered subject, the research question in the words the student is currently using, the last comment the supervisor made, and the school's internal draft deadline. Those four answers decide the match more than anything else a parent can tell us.

The registered subject matters far more than most parents expect. An Extended Essay in History is read for the handling of sources and the weighing of competing interpretations. One in Biology is read for method, data handling and the honesty of the evaluation. One in English is read for the quality of the reading of the text itself. A tutor who is confident about essay structure in general but has never worked through an Economics Extended Essay will give advice that sounds entirely sensible and scores nothing, because the criteria reward subject-specific reasoning rather than tidy paragraphs. We filter on the subject group first and treat writing craft as the second filter, never the first.

Most parents reach us having already typed "best IB tutor in Mumbai" or "IB tutors near me Mumbai" into Google, which is a sensible place to start and a poor place to finish, because neither phrase tells a search engine which subject group the essay is registered in. The second question is where the student actually stands. "Has a question and cannot start" is a different brief from "has eleven pages of notes and no argument", which is different again from "has an overlong draft and three weeks left". Each of those needs a different first session, and a tutor who is good at the third is not automatically good at the first. The third question is domestic: which suburb, which evenings are genuinely free once school and sport are accounted for, whether the study table is shared with a younger sibling, and whether your building wants a visitor pass arranged ahead of a standing weekly slot.

There is one kind of request we turn down at this stage. If the message is "can someone write the conclusion" or "can someone sort the draft out before Friday", we say no on the call and explain why. A tutor may teach a skill, press on a draft with questions, and mark that draft against the published criteria. A tutor may never write, redraft, research for, supply data for, or produce any part of an Extended Essay or an Internal Assessment. The student signs the work as their own, so the work has to be theirs.

2. We shortlist two or three IB specialists from that subject group
3. A short call covers the draft stage, free evenings and building access
4. First session: the student reads their own draft aloud against the criteria
5. Confirm a standing weekly slot, or we shortlist a different tutor

sections.heading: Where the Extended Essay sits in the IB Diploma Programme (DP) in Mumbai
paragraphs: The Extended Essay (EE) is the independent research essay every candidate in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) writes, and it sits in the DP core alongside Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the creativity, activity and service requirement. We deliberately do not quote how the core converts into points, how long the essay may run, or how many supervisor meetings are required, because the IB revises its guides on its own cycle and the only rules that matter are the ones in the guide your child is registered under. Your school's Diploma Programme coordinator has that document and will give you the current version in a two-minute conversation.

What we can describe is the shape of the two years as Mumbai families actually experience it. The subject is chosen and the question drafted in DP1, usually after the school runs an introductory session on what research at this level means. The research and the first full draft land across the long gap between DP1 ending and DP2 beginning. The redrafting, the reflections and the final submission fall in DP2, in the same months as the heaviest Internal Assessment (IA) deadlines. A student who leaves the essay until DP2 has not left themselves a hard job; they have left themselves three hard jobs stacked on one calendar.

The supervisor is appointed by the school, and so is the subject teacher. That is not a formality we are being polite about. The supervisor is the only person whose comments count inside the school's process, the only person who signs off on the authenticity of the work, and the only person who can tell a student what their own school expects at each internal checkpoint. A tutor working alongside that relationship never replaces it, never overrides it and never contacts the school. If a tutor's advice and the supervisor's advice disagree, the supervisor wins and the tutor's job is to help the student understand why.

The essay may be registered in a subject the student takes at Higher Level (HL) or at Standard Level (SL), and it may be registered in a subject with constraints a student has not noticed. That is a question for the coordinator rather than for us, and it is worth asking early, because changing the registered subject late is the single most expensive change a candidate can make.
bullets: The Extended Essay sits in the DP core with Theory of Knowledge (TOK)
Subject and question in DP1; redrafting and reflections land in DP2
The school appoints the supervisor and signs off authenticity, not a tutor
Ask the DP coordinator for the current guide instead of trusting any website
Changing the registered subject late is the costliest possible change

sections.heading: Subject choice, the research question and what the criteria actually reward
paragraphs: Three decisions set the ceiling on an Extended Essay before a single paragraph is written: which subject it is registered in, how narrow the question is, and whether the student can get at the material the question demands. A question about a famous equity market crash sounds exciting until the student discovers the data series they need sits behind a subscription. A question about a local Mumbai manufacturer sounds modest until it turns out the student can obtain real figures and ask real questions, at which point it outperforms the exciting one comfortably.

The criteria are published, they are named in the current guide, and they are the only standard that matters. Broadly they reward a focused question with a method suited to it, genuine subject knowledge used rather than displayed, critical thinking applied to the student's own evidence, presentation that lets a reader follow the argument, and honest engagement with how the work actually went. We teach students to read those criteria as instructions rather than as a rubric to be shown at the end, because almost every weak draft we see is a draft written to a topic rather than to a criterion.

The reflections on planning and progress are part of the assessment, not paperwork attached to it. They are written by the student, in the student's voice, about what they actually tried, abandoned and changed. A reflection that says "I learned a lot about time management" is wasted space. One that says "the first two sources agreed so completely that I went looking for a third that did not, and the third changed the structure of section two" does real work, because it shows a mind in motion. A tutor who drafts those sentences has manufactured an authenticity problem rather than solved one.

Marking a student's own draft is the most useful thing a session can do, and it is also where the boundary is clearest. The student brings the draft. The tutor asks what criterion each section is trying to satisfy, points at the paragraph where the argument stops advancing, and explains which band the draft currently sits in and why. The tutor does not rewrite the paragraph, supply the missing analysis, or hand over a corrected version. The student goes away and writes the next draft, which is the only version anybody is interested in.
bullets: Narrow questions with reachable material beat ambitious questions with none
Read the published criteria as instructions before drafting, not after
Reflections are assessed: the student's own voice, actual changes, no ghosting
A tutor names the band and the reason; the student writes the next draft
Subject knowledge has to be used in the argument, not displayed beside it

sections.heading: Which parts of Mumbai we cover for IB DP Extended Essay home tuition
paragraphs: We match tutors for IB DP Extended Essay home tuition in Mumbai across all six zones of the city, and we match within a zone wherever we can, because a tutor who can reach you in twenty minutes keeps a weekly slot for a full term and a tutor crossing the city does not. In the Western Suburbs, which carry the largest share of DP candidates in Mumbai, Maharashtra, we place tutors along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway rather than across them: Bandra to Khar West to Santacruz works, Juhu to Andheri works, Malad to Kandivali to Borivali works, and Dahisar sits comfortably on Metro Lines 2A and 7. Goregaon East off the JVLR is its own pocket, reached by road rather than by rail.

South Mumbai is short-distance and slow. A tutor moving from Worli to Colaba covers a handful of kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at seven in the evening, so we match inside the island rather than pulling somebody down from the suburbs. Cuffe Parade, Fort, Walkeshwar, Babulnath and Tardeo are all served by island-based tutors; the Coastal Road has changed the Worli and Nariman Point run noticeably, and Metro Line 3 has changed the Cuffe Parade to Bandra Kurla Complex trip more than the map suggests.

In the Central Suburbs we cover Powai, Chandivali, Kurla, Kanjurmarg and Ghatkopar, with Powai as the awkward case: it is physically central and has no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Ghatkopar or Kanjurmarg over the JVLR, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road matters to anybody crossing from the Western side. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup up to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines and the Eastern Express Highway, and the Eastern Freeway makes Wadala and Chembur far closer to the island than they look.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so we match node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short run from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and the Atal Setu has shortened the island crossing without making a weekday evening commute from South Mumbai realistic for a full term. In Thane, the Ghodbunder Road stretch sets the schedule: a tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, so we place Thane tutors in Thane, across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Hiranandani Estate, with Mulund tutors crossing over only when the slot is late enough to clear the worst of it.

sections.heading: How do Mumbai school EE deadlines land across DP1 and DP2?
paragraphs: Mumbai schools set their own internal Extended Essay checkpoints well ahead of the external submission, which is why two students in the same building can be under completely different pressure in the same week. Most schools here want a question signed off before the long break at the end of DP1, a full first draft early in DP2, and a final version weeks before anything is actually sent anywhere. The internal deadline is the one that governs your household calendar, and it is the one parents most often do not know.

Families we work with attend schools including Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in Bandra Kurla Complex, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off the JVLR in Goregaon East, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, B.D. Somani International School at Cuffe Parade, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, the JBCN International School campuses at Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. Naming a school here is local context and nothing more. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, nor with the International Baccalaureate organisation.

The collision that catches DP2 families is not the Extended Essay on its own. It is the fortnight where an Extended Essay redraft, two Internal Assessment deadlines and a mock paper land together, often in the same month as a TOK exhibition or essay. A student in Chembur with a Physics IA draft due the same week as her Extended Essay redraft does not have a motivation problem; she has a sequencing problem, and the fix is deciding which one gets the good hours and which one gets the leftovers.

That is the argument for starting during DP1 rather than in the panic window. The students who finish calmly are almost always the ones whose question was settled and whose reading was done before DP2 began, which leaves DP2 for the work that actually earns marks: redrafting, cutting and sharpening. Ask your school for its internal checkpoint dates in writing and put them on the same calendar as the IA deadlines, because seeing the stack is what changes behaviour.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for the Extended Essay writing phase?
paragraphs: Home tuition is what most Mumbai families book for this work and it is what we lead with. The Extended Essay (EE) home classes Mumbai parents ask for are almost always a single protected weekly sitting at the student's own desk rather than a course of lessons. IB DP Extended Essay home tuition in Mumbai means a tutor at your dining table with the student's draft printed out, pens on the page, and the criteria open beside it. For the writing phase specifically this is the strongest format, because the session is built on reading the student's own sentences slowly and asking what each one is doing. That is hard to do well over a screen share, and it is much harder to fake: a parent in the next room hears whether a session is teaching or dictating.

Online suits a narrow set of situations genuinely well. An IB online tutor in Mumbai is the better answer when the registered subject is unusual enough that the right specialist lives in a different zone, when the student is at a boarding school or travelling, or when the slot that actually works is early on a Sunday. Screen-shared drafts with tracked comments are fine for structural feedback, and recorded sessions help a student who needs to hear the same point twice. The honest trade-off is attention: a seventeen-year-old with a phone beside the laptop at nine in the evening is not fully in the room.

Hybrid is what most of our Extended Essay placements settle into by DP2. One home session a week for the hard, slow work of reading and marking a draft, plus a short online check-in mid-week to confirm the student actually wrote the thing they said they would write. Hybrid also absorbs the Mumbai problem that no scheduling cleverness fixes: monsoon weeks, exam weeks, and the evenings when Ghodbunder Road or the Western Express Highway simply does not move. The session happens online instead of not happening.

Whichever mode you choose, the boundary does not move with it. Online or at your table, a tutor teaches technique, questions a draft and marks it against the published criteria. A tutor does not write sentences into the document, does not research the topic on the student's behalf, does not supply data, and does not produce any part of the submission. If a tutor offers to "just tidy it up" in a shared document, that is the point to stop the engagement and tell us.
bullets: Home tuition suits the writing phase: printed draft, criteria open, slow reading
Online fits scarce subjects, travel, boarding school and early weekend slots
Hybrid is common in DP2: one home session plus a mid-week online check
Online sessions lose attention more than they lose content

sections.heading: How are IB home tutors in Mumbai checked before they reach your door?
paragraphs: Before a tutor appears on a shortlist for IB DP Extended Essay home tuition in Mumbai we confirm identity with government photo identification, we confirm the subject claim with degree documents or examiner or teaching evidence in that subject, and we take references we can actually call rather than a line in a profile. For Extended Essay work we also ask something more specific: which subjects they have supervised or marked research writing in, and what they tell a student who asks them to fix a draft. The second answer is more informative than the first.

What we check is not everything a parent should check. Ask the tutor directly, in the first session and in front of your child, what they will not do. The answer you want is plain: they will not write, redraft, research for or supply data for the essay, and they will not touch the document. A tutor who hesitates, or who answers with something about "guiding the writing", has told you what you need to know. A tutor who says it cleanly has just made your child's authenticity declaration easier to sign honestly.

Those two questions are the whole difference between an IB home tutor in Mumbai who is useful and one who is a risk, and they cost nothing to ask. The other checks are practical. Ask how the tutor will record what happened in each session, because a short written note after each sitting is the record that protects everybody if the school ever asks how the essay was produced. Ask whether they are willing for you to keep every dated draft in one folder. Ask whether they expect to contact the school, and expect the answer to be no, because the supervisor relationship belongs to the school and a tutor inserting themselves into it causes problems rather than solving them.

Be wary of anybody who promises a specific grade, offers a sample essay "to work from", or quotes a package price for an outcome rather than for sessions. Those three signals travel together. An honest Extended Essay tutor will tell you plainly that the result depends on what the student does between sessions, and will be comfortable with you sitting in on a session to see how it runs.

Ask the tutor in session one, out loud, what they will refuse to do
Keep every dated draft in one folder and a short note per session

sections.heading: Writing at length: one argument instead of ten separate sections
paragraphs: The hardest part of the Extended Essay is not producing enough words. It is making one argument hold across the whole length of the piece. Most first drafts that reach us are sequences of competent sections, each answering a slightly different question, so the essay reads as a set of short essays sharing a title page. The reader is looking for a line of reasoning that starts in the opening paragraph and is still being pushed forward on the last page. Stamina produces length. Structure produces marks, and the two are not the same problem.

The test we teach is applied one paragraph at a time, out loud. What does this paragraph do for the argument that the previous paragraph did not already do? If the only honest answer is "it says more about the topic", the paragraph is description, and description is where marks quietly disappear. A student in Khar West writing on wartime propaganda can describe twelve posters and score below a student who analyses three, because the third one complicates the pattern the first two suggested, and showing that complication is the thinking the criteria reward.

We teach the introduction written last. It is the one section that has to promise precisely what the essay delivers, and nobody knows what the essay delivers until it exists. Signposting earns marks only when it is honest and specific: "this section tests the first explanation against the second data set" is a signpost, while "now we will look at some other factors" is filler that costs space. The conclusion has to answer the question actually printed on the title page, including answering it partially, or with a qualification, if that is where the evidence landed. A conclusion that quietly answers an easier question is the most common way a strong draft loses marks late.

Editing down an overlong draft is a real skill and it belongs to the student. A tutor can show how to spot the paragraph that repeats an earlier one in new clothes, how to compress three sentences of setup into a single clause, and where a long block quotation should become a short quotation plus a sentence of analysis. The tutor demonstrates the move on a different passage, and the student makes the cuts in their own document. That division is not a technicality. It is the difference between a student who can explain every decision in the essay when asked and a student who cannot, and being able to explain every decision is the best protection a candidate has.
bullets: Read each paragraph aloud and name what it adds that the last one did not
Write the introduction last, once the essay's real claim has settled
Signpost with the specific test the next section runs, never with filler
Cut repetition and setup before cutting evidence when a draft runs long
The tutor demonstrates a cut elsewhere; the student cuts their own document

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and submission
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a better draft. You should expect a sharper question, a plan the student can say out loud without reading it, and a visible change in how they talk about their own work. The clearest early signal is the student using the language of the criteria unprompted, saying "this bit is description" about their own paragraph. If after four weeks the student still cannot explain what their essay argues in two sentences, something is wrong with the match and we would rather hear from you then than in month three.

At one term the draft should be doing structural work: an argument that runs end to end, sections that each advance it, evidence used rather than listed, and a student who knows which parts are weak. Expect the draft to be too long at this stage, because a draft that is already the right length after one term is usually a draft that has not explored enough. By the end of a term the reflections should be accumulating as the student goes, written at the time, rather than being reconstructed from memory the week before submission.

By submission the honest measure is simple: can the student explain every decision in the essay, in their own words, without the tutor in the room? If yes, the work is theirs and the process was sound, whatever the eventual mark. We do not guarantee grades and nobody honestly can, because the result depends on the student's reading, their writing between sessions and an external process none of us controls. What a good tutor changes is the quality of the thinking the student brings to the page, and that is worth paying for on its own terms.

When a match is not working, tell us early and tell us specifically: the student has stopped preparing, the sessions have become the tutor talking, or the feedback is vague. We re-shortlist from the same subject group and hand over the session notes so the new tutor does not start from zero. The one thing we will not do is keep a placement alive because the calendar is tight. If a tutor has begun drifting towards writing or correcting the draft directly, that placement ends immediately, whatever month it is.
bullets: Four weeks: a sharper question and criteria language used unprompted
One term: an argument running end to end, and a deliberately overlong draft
Reflections written as the work happens, not reconstructed at the end
We do not guarantee grades; the student's work between sessions decides most of it
Vague feedback or a tutor touching the draft ends the placement at once

sections.heading: Starting IB DP Extended Essay home tuition in Mumbai this term
paragraphs: To get a shortlist that is actually useful, send four things: the registered subject, the research question as it currently reads, the school's next internal deadline, and your suburb with the evenings that are genuinely free. If the student has a draft, send its length and nothing else about it; we do not want the document and a tutor will read it with the student rather than before them. If there is no draft, say what exists instead, whether that is a reading list, a page of notes or an empty file. Say also whether you want an IB private tutor Mumbai side of the creek or across it, because a home tutor for Extended Essay (EE) Mumbai families book in Vashi is a different shortlist from one in Worli.

The first session is diagnostic and it is deliberately uncomfortable. The student explains the question in their own words, says what they think the essay will argue, and reads one paragraph of whatever they have written aloud. The tutor maps that against the published criteria and names, concretely, the two things that would improve the draft most. The student leaves with a task for the week that they will do alone, because a session that ends with the tutor taking work away has already gone wrong.

What we will not take on, stated once more because these requests arrive weekly: we do not write Extended Essays or Internal Assessments, we do not redraft them, we do not research them, we do not supply data for them, and we do not accept work framed as finishing or fixing a submission. If artificial intelligence tools have been used at any point, that use is declared under the school's own rules, and a tutor will tell a student to go and declare it rather than help them around it. Those limits are the service, not a restriction on it.

Practically, a standing weekly slot works better than a block of sessions booked in a panic. Pick a day and time your household can protect for a term, tell us about the building's visitor protocol before the first visit, and let the tutor and student settle into a rhythm. The essays that land well are almost never the ones rescued late; they are the ones worked on steadily by a student who understood, early, that this is their piece of writing and nobody else's.
bullets: Send subject, question, next internal deadline, suburb and free evenings
First session: the student explains the question and reads a paragraph aloud
Every session ends with work for the student, never work for the tutor
Declare any AI use under the school's rules; a tutor will insist on it

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Khar West for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Khar West it is usually straightforward because we match along the Western Line rather than across the city. A tutor based between Bandra and Santacruz reaches most Khar West buildings in fifteen to twenty minutes outside the worst of the evening peak, so a 7pm or 7.30pm start on a fixed weekday holds for a full term. What breaks these slots is not distance but crossing the Western Express Highway at the wrong hour. Tell us your two preferred evenings and we will shortlist tutors who live on your side of the line.

faqs.question: Our society in Powai requires a gate pass for every visitor. How does that work?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once with your society office as a recurring weekly visitor and the problem disappears. In Powai and the larger Hiranandani Gardens complexes this is routine, and most managements will issue a standing entry for a named tutor on a fixed day once a resident sponsors it. Give us the building's requirement before the first visit so the tutor carries photo identification that matches the name on the pass. Where a society insists on a fresh pass each time, we ask the tutor to arrive ten minutes early rather than losing session time at the gate.

faqs.question: Can you help finish my daughter's Extended Essay? It is due in ten days.
faqs.answer: We cannot finish it, and no honest service can. What a tutor can do in ten days is sit with your daughter, read what exists against the published criteria, tell her which two changes would improve it most, and teach her how to make those changes herself in the time left. What a tutor will not do is write a section, rewrite her paragraphs, add research, or hand back a corrected document. She signs the essay as her own work, and a submission she did not write puts her entire diploma at risk, not just one essay. If the request is really "produce a finished essay", we will decline the work.

faqs.question: Will a tutor polish the draft or correct the English in it?
faqs.answer: No. Polishing somebody else's academic submission is producing part of it, whatever it is called. A tutor will tell your son that paragraph four repeats paragraph two, that a sentence is doing three jobs and should do one, and that a tense slips in his methods section, and will show him how to fix that kind of problem on a different passage. He then makes the corrections in his own document. The reason is not pedantry: a student who made every edit himself can explain every sentence if the school asks, and a student handed a cleaned-up file cannot.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Rates for IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on five things rather than a published price list: the board and level, how scarce the subject specialism is, how far the tutor travels and at what hour, the session length, and whether you book home sessions, online or a hybrid pattern. Extended Essay work in a common subject group costs less to staff than a scarce one, and a South Mumbai evening slot that needs a tutor to cross Peddar Road in peak hour prices differently from a slot ten minutes away. We quote per tutor once we know those details, and we do not quote an outcome.

faqs.question: My son already has a supervisor at school. Why would he also need a tutor?
faqs.answer: The supervisor is appointed by the school, owns the process and signs off the work, and nothing a tutor does replaces that. The gap a tutor fills is time and repetition. A supervisor has a limited number of meetings with a limited number of minutes each, spread across several candidates, while the writing problem your son has is one he needs to work on weekly with somebody reading his sentences slowly. A tutor also never contacts the school. If supervisor advice and tutor advice conflict, the supervisor is right and the tutor's job is to help him understand the reasoning.

faqs.question: The research question feels far too broad. Can a tutor narrow it for him?
faqs.answer: A tutor can press on it until he narrows it himself, which is a different and more useful thing. The session looks like interrogation: what exactly are you comparing, over what period, using what evidence, and what would a surprising answer look like? Most broad questions collapse into something workable in forty minutes of that. The tutor does not hand over a replacement question, partly because a question the student did not choose produces an essay he cannot sustain for the full length, and partly because the question is part of the work he is submitting as his own.

faqs.question: How many sessions does the writing phase usually take?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the student starts, and we will not invent a number for your case. A student with a settled question, a full set of notes and a clear argument may need a handful of sessions on structure and cutting. A student who has drifted for a term needs weekly sessions across months, because the problem is not the draft but the habit of working on it. The useful way to plan is a standing weekly slot through to the school's internal deadline, reviewed after four weeks when there is actual evidence of how fast this particular student moves.

faqs.question: Does online work for Extended Essay sessions, or is home tuition better?
faqs.answer: For the writing phase, home tuition is better and we say so plainly. Reading a draft slowly, pen on paper, with the criteria open beside it, is a physical activity that loses something over a screen share. Online is the right answer when the registered subject is scarce enough that the right specialist is in another zone, when the student is travelling, or when the only workable slot is an early Sunday. Most families end up hybrid by DP2: one home session for the hard reading and a short online check mid-week to confirm the writing actually happened.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What happens then?
faqs.answer: Tell us, with specifics, and we re-shortlist from the same subject group. The useful specifics are these: has the student stopped preparing between sessions, have the sessions become the tutor talking while the student listens, or is the feedback too vague to act on? Each points to a different fix, and only the third is always the tutor's fault. We hand the session notes to the next tutor so nothing restarts from zero. We will not keep a placement running because a deadline is close, and we end it immediately if a tutor has started editing the draft directly.

faqs.question: Is artificial intelligence allowed? My daughter used it to summarise some articles.
faqs.answer: That use must be declared under your school's own rules, and the school's policy is the one that governs, not ours. Schools in Mumbai differ on what is permitted and on how it is recorded, so the first step is reading your school's academic honesty policy and then telling the supervisor exactly what was used and for what. A tutor will tell her to declare it rather than help her work around it, and will not use these tools to produce or improve any part of her essay. An undeclared use discovered later is treated as misconduct against the candidate.

faqs.question: Should the tutor speak to the supervisor or email the school about the essay?
faqs.answer: No, and we instruct tutors not to. The supervisor and the subject teacher are appointed by the school, the relationship belongs to the school, and a private tutor inserting themselves into it creates confusion about who is advising the candidate. If something needs raising with the school, you or your child raise it. The tutor's contribution is to make sure your child walks into the next supervisor meeting able to say clearly what the essay argues, what changed since last time, and what they want feedback on.

The subject is chosen, the supervisor has been appointed by the school, and the student has three weeks of notes that do not add up to an answerable question. What that student needs is not a writer. She needs someone who sits beside her for an hour a week and teaches the research method the essay is actually assessed on, then leaves her to do the reading.

A tutor may teach research skills, question a draft the student has written, and mark that draft against the published criteria so the student knows where it stands. A tutor may never write, redraft, research for, or produce any part of an Extended Essay. The student signs the essay as her own work, so it has to be her own work. sections.heading: Where the Extended Essay sits in the Diploma Programme
paragraphs: The Extended Essay (EE) is one of the core requirements of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), sitting alongside Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the creativity, activity, service strand. It is an independent piece of research in a subject the student chooses, written over a long stretch of DP1 and finished in DP2, and it is supervised inside the school by a teacher the school appoints. Nobody outside the school replaces that supervisor, and a tutor working with your child does not contact the school.

Because the essay is independent, the research phase is the part of it that is genuinely unsupervised in practice. A student gets scheduled reflection sessions with her supervisor and a Reflections on Planning and Progress Form to complete, and between those sessions she is on her own with a reading list she has to build herself. That gap is where a tutor is legitimately useful, and it is also where families get into trouble, because the easiest way to close a gap in reading is to let somebody else do it.

Word limits, submission dates and the exact structure of the supervised reflections are set in the current subject guide and by your school's DP coordinator, and the IB revises its guides on its own cycle. We will not quote those details to you from memory. Ask your coordinator for the version that applies to your child's session, then build the schedule backwards from it. A tutor who tells you the requirements without checking which guide is current is guessing.

An Extended Essay (EE) IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai families book for a standing weekly slot is usually brought in during DP1, when the question is still movable. Bringing someone in during the last fortnight of DP2 is a different and much worse conversation, and it is one we have most weeks. At that stage the honest options are narrow, legitimate and unglamorous, and we will say so.

sections.heading: Choosing a subject, then building a question the evidence can answer
paragraphs: Subject choice decides how hard the research will be, and most students choose on affection rather than on feasibility. A student who loves Economics but has no access to firm-level data will spend two months failing to find numbers. A student who picks Biology and wants fieldwork needs a site she can reach on a Saturday morning from Chembur or Kandivali East, not a coral reef. The first useful thing a tutor does is make the student test her subject choice against what she can actually read, reach and measure from where she lives.

The research question comes second and matters more. Broad questions feel safe and are the commonest reason an essay reads thin: a question about the effects of colonialism on Indian textiles has no boundary, while a question about how one mill's output was recorded across two specific decades has one. A tutor's job here is to press on scope until the question is narrow enough that evidence exists for it, and then to check that the evidence is in a language the student reads and a format she can cite.

The published criteria reward focus and method, subject knowledge, critical thinking, presentation, and the engagement a student shows in her reflections. Almost all of those are decided during research, not during writing. A student who kept a dated log of searches, dead ends and decisions can write a reflection that sounds like a researcher. A student who read for six weeks without recording anything has to reconstruct it, and reconstruction reads exactly like reconstruction to an examiner.

A tutor can model all of this on a different topic. He can show the student how he would narrow a question in his own field, how he would judge a source he had not seen before, and how he would record a citation. He may not do any of it on her topic, because that would be research for her essay. The line is simple to hold once it is stated out loud: the method is taught, the work is hers, and the essay she signs is the one she wrote.

sections.heading: How do Mumbai school EE deadlines fall across the year?
paragraphs: Mumbai IB schools set their own internal Extended Essay milestones inside the IB's outer deadline, and those internal dates are what actually govern your term. Typically a subject and a draft question are fixed late in DP1, a first full draft is wanted before or just after the DP1 to DP2 break, and the final submission lands in DP2 alongside Internal Assessments and mock examinations. Your school's DP coordinator publishes the real calendar; everything a tutor plans should be pinned to it rather than to a general assumption.

Families we work with attend Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in Bandra Kurla Complex, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off the JVLR, B.D. Somani International School at Cuffe Parade, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, JBCN International School in Chembur, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Thakur International School in Kandivali East and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. Naming them is context about the calendar pressure you are under. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named here and not affiliated with the International Baccalaureate organisation.

The pressure point that catches most Mumbai students is not the final deadline. It is the first full draft, because it usually falls in the same six weeks as two Internal Assessment drafts and the TOK essay, and it is the first time the thinness of the research shows. A student who did her reading properly across DP1 writes that draft in a fortnight. A student who did not spends the fortnight reading instead, and then has no time to write.

The monsoon weeks between June and September are the other quiet problem. Sessions get cancelled, a tutor coming from Ghatkopar to Powai loses an hour to standing water on the JVLR, and a project with no fixed weekly slot simply stops. We plan a makeup rule into the schedule at the start of the term instead of improvising one in August.

sections.heading: Home classes, online sessions, or a mix for EE research?
paragraphs: Home is the default and we lead with it. An IB DP extended essay home tutor in Mumbai sits at the same table as the student, can see the pile of printouts, the half-filled log and the browser tabs, and can stop a bad search habit in the moment it happens. For a student who has drifted, physical presence is also a commitment device: somebody is arriving at seven on Thursday whether or not the reading is done. Home tuition in Mumbai costs travel time, so the slot has to be geographically honest or it lapses by week six.

Online suits the parts of this project that are screen work. Searching a database, checking whether a journal article is accessible, formatting a reference, reading a student's own notes back to her: all of that works as well on a shared screen as in a room, and an IB online tutor in Mumbai can be matched on subject rather than on postcode, which matters when the essay is in a subject with few specialists in the city. The trade-off is attention. A fifteen-year-old alone in a bedroom with a shared screen is easier to lose than one at the dining table.

The mix most of our EE families settle on is a fortnightly home session for the hard conversations and a short online check-in in the alternate week to keep the log moving. Whether you book Extended Essay (EE) home classes Mumbai tutors travel to, or online sessions, or both, the structure of the work is the same: the student reads between sessions, brings what she found, and defends her choices. Nothing about the mode changes what a tutor may do.

It changes what a tutor can be tempted to do, though, which is worth saying plainly. Online work puts a tutor's cursor near the student's document, and a tutor who starts typing in that file has crossed the line even if the words are small. Our rule in both modes is that the student holds the keyboard. A tutor may ask a question against a paragraph, name the criterion it is failing, and say nothing more until the student has rewritten it herself.

sections.heading: How are IB DP Extended Essay home tutors in Mumbai checked?
paragraphs: Before a tutor appears on a shortlist we check three things: identity, subject credential, and whether the person has actually supervised or examined research at this level rather than only taught the subject. For an Extended Essay the third matters most, because a strong Chemistry teacher is not automatically someone who can tell a student that her question has no obtainable data. An IB DP extended essay home tutor in Mumbai who cannot describe how he would narrow a question in his own field does not get listed.

We also ask every tutor to state the boundary back to us in his own words before his first booking. If the answer includes any version of writing a section, supplying a reference list, or cleaning up a draft on the student's behalf, the application stops there. The permitted work is teaching skills, questioning what the student has written, and marking her draft against the published criteria so she can see where she stands. Producing text is not on the list in any form.

There is a parallel list of things you should check yourself, and it takes one conversation. Ask the tutor which subject he studied and at what level. Ask him what he would do in the first session if your child arrived with no sources at all. Ask him how he records what the student did between sessions. Then ask him directly what he will not do, and listen for whether the boundary comes out as a clear rule or as a vague reassurance. Be wary of anyone who promises a specific grade, and be wary of anyone who offers to take a look at the draft and send it back improved. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will either.

Keep the paperwork light but real. We ask families to confirm the weekly slot in writing, to note cancellations as they happen, and to tell us at four weeks whether the student is doing more of the work than she was at the start. That last question is the only reliable measure of whether the help is the legitimate kind.

sections.heading: Finding sources a Mumbai student can actually reach
paragraphs: This is the phase where Extended Essays are won or lost, and it is almost never the phase families ask about. Start with what the student already has: the school library, which in most Mumbai IB schools includes subscription databases a student can reach with her own login and which she has usually never opened. A tutor's first legitimate job is to sit with her while she logs in, searches badly, and is shown why the search was bad. Teaching the search is the work. Running the search for her is not.

Beyond school, the city has public and university reading collections, and the honest advice is to find out what access exists rather than to assume. The older research libraries around Fort and Kala Ghoda hold material that is not online at all, and some university departments allow supervised reading on application; both are worth a phone call before an afternoon trip from Powai or Thane. Open-access routes matter more for most students: a subject-specific open repository, a national open archive, a government statistics portal, or the author's own institutional page. When a key article is paywalled, the legitimate moves are to look for an author-deposited version, to check whether an open repository holds the accepted manuscript, to write to the author and ask, or to decide the essay does not need that article. Paying for a single article is a last resort and rarely necessary.

Judging quality is harder than finding things, because the student is new to the field and has no instinct for who is credible in it. We teach a short set of checks she can apply herself: who published it and does that publisher review what it prints, when was it written and has the field moved, what evidence does it cite, and who cites it. A tutor can walk through those checks on a source in his own subject and then hand her three sources in hers to judge out loud. She reaches the verdict. He says whether her reasoning holds.

Two habits save the whole project. First, record the full reference at the moment you first open a source, in the format your school requires, with the page you took the idea from. Reconstructing citations in the last week is where honest students accidentally become dishonest ones, because a half-remembered source gets cited from memory. Second, keep a dated research log: what you searched, what you found, what you rejected and why. The log feeds the reflections directly, and it gives the student something true to say about her own thinking. It also tells you when to change course. If three weeks of competent searching has produced no evidence, the question is wrong, not the student, and a tutor who says so in week five has saved her the essay. A home tutor for Extended Essay (EE) Mumbai students book in DP1 has time to make that call; one booked in DP2 does not.

sections.heading: What a tutor will never do, and what progress looks like
paragraphs: It is worth repeating the boundary in the plainest terms available, because this is a search people make for the wrong reason. A tutor may teach research and writing skills, ask hard questions about a draft the student has produced, and mark that draft against the published criteria. A tutor may never write, redraft, research for, or produce any part of an Extended Essay. The student submits it as her own work and signs a declaration to that effect. If AI tools are used at any stage, their use is declared under the school's own rules, and the student is the one who declares it. IB Gram will not accept work framed as producing or fixing a submission, whatever the deadline is.

Within those limits, here is what to expect. At four weeks the visible change is organisational rather than textual: there is a research log with dates in it, a reference list that was built as she read, and a question that is narrower than the one she started with. She can also explain to you, without notes, why two sources she found are better than three she rejected. If none of that is true at four weeks, something is wrong and we would rather hear from you than not.

At one term the question is settled, the reading is largely done, and she has an outline that maps evidence to each section. By one full exam cycle, the essay is a finished piece of work she can defend in a viva-style conversation with her supervisor, and the skills have spread: students who learn to log and cite properly for the Extended Essay stop losing marks on Internal Assessments for the same reasons. The grade itself depends on her work, her school's teaching and the examiner's judgement, and we do not guarantee grades.

Our honest limits are worth stating too. A tutor cannot manufacture evidence that does not exist for a question the student will not give up. He cannot replace six months of reading in three weeks. He cannot sit the viva. And if a family's real request turns out to be that someone else produce the essay, there is no version of our service that meets it, which is a better thing to hear from us in week one than from a school in week forty.

sections.heading: Starting with an IB home tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Getting started takes one message and about ten minutes of preparation on your side. Tell us the essay subject, whether your child is in DP1 or DP2, your locality and the two weekly slots that genuinely work in your household. Then send three things if they exist: the research question as currently written, the supervisor's most recent written comment, and a list of whatever sources the student has so far, even if it is four links and a screenshot. Families searching for IB tutors near me Mumbai usually have the first and none of the rest, which is fine.

The first session is ninety minutes and it is diagnostic. The tutor asks the student to explain the question aloud, looks at what she has read, and finds out whether the problem is the question, the sources, the note-taking or the drift. He then writes a one-page research plan: what to search, where, in what order, and what to bring next week. The student leaves with homework that is reading and logging, not writing. You get the same plan by email so you know what was agreed.

If you want to compare before committing, ask for two profiles and speak to both. The questions that separate a research tutor from a subject teacher are narrow: how do you narrow a question, how do you handle a paywalled source, and what will you refuse to do. A good tutor answers the third one fastest. Whether you end up booking IB home tuition in Mumbai, online sessions, or a fortnightly mix, the first session looks the same.

What we will not do is take a booking that is really a request for someone to produce an essay. If the enquiry arrives the week before submission asking for a tidy-up, we will tell you what is legitimately possible in that window, which is usually proofreading advice the student applies herself and a frank conversation about the declaration she has to sign. An IB private tutor Mumbai parents hire for the last seven days cannot fix a year of missing research, and anyone who says otherwise is selling you a risk to your child's diploma.

faqs.question: What exactly will an Extended Essay tutor do, and what will they not do?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches method, questions your child's own draft, and marks it against the published criteria; a tutor never writes, redrafts, researches for, or produces any part of the essay. In practice that means showing her how to search a database, how to judge whether a source is credible, how to log what she did, and how to read her own paragraph against a criterion. It does not mean supplying sources, drafting a paragraph to show her how, or rewriting her introduction. She signs the essay as her own work, so it has to be hers.

faqs.question: My daughter has asked for help to finish and polish her Extended Essay before the deadline. Will you do that?
faqs.answer: No. We will not finish, polish, rewrite or research an Extended Essay, and we do not take bookings framed that way. What we will do in that window is read nothing and ask her to talk us through what she has, teach her how to check her own referencing and formatting against her school's requirements, show her how to read each section against the relevant criterion so she can cut and fix it herself, and help her plan the hours she has left. Every edit is typed by her. If what is wanted is text produced by someone else, we are the wrong service and we will say so on the call.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Kharghar for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if the tutor is matched inside Navi Mumbai rather than brought across the creek. Kharghar sits a short drive from Belapur and Panvel along the Sion-Panvel Highway, so a Navi Mumbai tutor holds a 7pm slot through a full term without difficulty. A tutor travelling from Bandra or Powai for the same slot will manage it in September and quietly start cancelling by November. We would rather match you node to node and keep the weekly rhythm, because a research project collapses when the sessions become irregular.

faqs.question: What does a tutor need from our society gate for a standing weekly home slot?
faqs.answer: A standing entry authorisation, arranged once rather than negotiated every week. Most Mumbai societies will add a recurring visitor to the register if a resident requests it in writing, and some ask for a photo identity record at the main gate. Give us the tutor's name as it appears on his identity document when you book so the two match, and tell us whether your building needs the resident to approve each entry through an app. Ten minutes of paperwork in week one prevents the twenty-minute delay that eats a quarter of a session in week nine.

faqs.question: Where should home sessions happen if the flat has no quiet study space?
faqs.answer: Anywhere with a table, a plug point and a door, which is usually the dining table after the kitchen has quietened down rather than a shared bedroom. Extended Essay work needs space to spread printouts and a screen open at the same time, so a desk the student cannot physically fit her reading onto is a real problem. Many Mumbai societies have a reading room or clubhouse table that residents can book; several of our Powai and Thane families use one for the first hour. Agree the room before the tutor arrives, not at the door.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for Extended Essay work?
faqs.answer: Mostly on the scarcity of the subject, the tutor's research credential, how far he travels and how long the session runs. An essay in a widely taught subject is easier to staff than one in a niche subject where the city has few specialists, and that scarcity shows up in the rate. Travel distance matters because a tutor crossing a zone is billing an hour of his evening he cannot bill to anyone else. Session length and frequency are yours to set. We quote per match rather than publishing a list, because a figure that fits Colaba and Panvel equally is a figure that fits neither.

faqs.question: How do we get a source when the key article is behind a paywall?
faqs.answer: Try four things in order before paying for anything. Check whether the author has deposited an accepted version in an open repository or on an institutional page; search the title for an open-access copy of the same manuscript; email the author directly, which works more often than students expect and is entirely legitimate; and check whether your school library's subscriptions already include the journal. If none of that works, the honest question is whether the essay genuinely needs that article. Often the answer is no, and a reachable source answers the same point.

faqs.question: Does the tutor speak to our school's Extended Essay supervisor?
faqs.answer: No. The supervisor is appointed by the school, owns the supervised reflection sessions and the official record of them, and a tutor neither replaces that relationship nor contacts the school. What a tutor does instead is make sure the student arrives at each reflection session able to say something true about her own progress. If the supervisor has written a comment, forward it to us and the tutor will work with it, but every message back to the school comes from your child or from you.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Tell us that week rather than at the end of the term. At four weeks the progress on an Extended Essay is not supposed to look like pages of text, so first check the right markers: is there a dated research log, has the reference list grown as she read, and has the question narrowed? If those three are missing, the sessions are not working and we rematch. If they are present and you were expecting prose, the project is probably on track and the expectation needs adjusting rather than the tutor.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Message us and we rematch, and you are not expected to justify it at length. The commonest reason an Extended Essay match fails is subject distance: the tutor knows the subject broadly but has never done research in the corner of it the student has chosen, so his questions stay general. The second commonest is pace. We ask what specifically did not work, because that answer changes the shortlist, then we send fresh profiles. Nothing about a rematch goes to the school, and your child's supervisor relationship is unaffected.

faqs.question: Is the research question allowed to change halfway through?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it often should, though the decision belongs to the student with her supervisor. If several weeks of competent searching has produced no usable evidence, the problem is the question, and narrowing or shifting it in DP1 costs far less than defending a thin essay in DP2. A tutor's role is to notice the pattern early and make the student articulate it: what did you search, what came back, what is genuinely missing. She then takes that to her supervisor. The tutor does not propose a replacement question for her to adopt.

faqs.question: Can my son use AI tools while researching his Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Only within your school's published rules, and any use he makes has to be declared by him. Schools differ in what they permit and the rules change, so the authority is your DP coordinator's current guidance, not a tutor's opinion. What a tutor will do is teach him the difference between a tool that helps him search and a tool that produces text he then submits, because the second one ends his diploma. Anything a model generates is not his work, and the declaration he signs says the essay is.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an online Extended Essay tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is the one piece of Diploma Programme work that is almost entirely written, almost entirely independent, and spread across a year. That combination is what makes it suit remote teaching better than nearly anything else a tutor does. There is no apparatus to set up, no board to write on, and no reason for two people to be in the same room while one of them reads a paragraph the other wrote last week. What there is, instead, is a document and a deadline that is too far away to feel real.

Our matching reflects that. 1. You send the essay subject, the year group and the two or three windows in the week when your child is actually free, including the odd twenty-minute slot you would not bother mentioning for a maths class. 2. We search the subject specialists first and the city second, because an online match does not need to live near you. 3. You get profiles showing each tutor's own research background and the shared-document workflow he uses. 4. Session one is run on screen with the student sharing her own document and her own search history. 5. We set a written rhythm for the term: when drafts are submitted, when comments come back, when the live sessions happen.

That rhythm is the part parents underestimate. A student who meets a tutor for ninety minutes a fortnight with nothing in between will arrive each time having done very little, because nothing was due. A student who knows a section goes into the shared document by Sunday evening and comes back annotated on Tuesday has a reason to write on Saturday. The sessions then start from marked work rather than from an apology.

One rule is fixed before the first booking and is stated to the student in session one. A tutor may teach skills, question what she has written and mark her draft against the published criteria. A tutor may never write, redraft, research for, or produce any part of an Extended Essay. She submits it as her own work and signs it as such, and any AI use is declared by her under her school's own rules. IB Gram does not take on enquiries framed as producing or fixing a submission, online or otherwise.

sections.heading: What the Diploma Programme asks of an independent researcher
paragraphs: The Extended Essay (EE) is a core requirement of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), alongside Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the service strand. The student picks a subject, frames her own question, does her own research and writes the essay across DP1 and DP2 with a supervisor the school appoints. That supervisor runs the scheduled reflection sessions and signs off the Reflections on Planning and Progress Form. No tutor replaces that person, and no tutor from IB Gram contacts your school.

The word the IB uses is independent, and it is meant literally. The assessment is interested in what the student can do unsupervised: hold a question, build an argument from evidence she chose, and account for her own decisions in writing. A remote tutor is a reasonable fit for this because remote work is structurally at arm's length. He cannot reach the keyboard. Everything he contributes has to arrive as a question, a comment or a judgement that the student then acts on by herself.

Submission dates, the word limit and the format of the supervised reflections come from the current subject guide and your school's DP coordinator. The IB revises guides on its own cycle, so we will not recite those details from memory and nor should any tutor you speak to. Get the current version, put the dates in a calendar the student can see, and work backwards. An Extended Essay (EE) IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai families book online can help build that backwards plan in the first session.

Worth separating two things families merge. The Extended Essay is not an Internal Assessment with a bigger word count. An Internal Assessment is tightly scaffolded by a subject teacher inside a syllabus. The Extended Essay hands the student the scaffolding problem itself, which is why a bright student who scores well on every IA can still produce a weak essay. It is a project-management failure more often than an intellectual one.

sections.heading: Subject choice, and the comment-by-comment work on a draft
paragraphs: Subject scarcity is the strongest argument for working online. A Mumbai student writing her Extended Essay in Economics or English has plenty of local options. A student writing in Philosophy, Psychology, Film, Global Politics, Music or a second language often does not, and the choice becomes a general IB tutor who will ask general questions or a specialist two time zones away who will ask the right ones. The specialist wins that comparison every time, and remote access is what makes him available at all.

Once a subject is fixed, the work becomes paragraph-level and it is well suited to written comments. A tutor reading a methodology section writes against the exact sentence that claims more than the evidence supports: what is your source for this, which of your three sources actually says it, and which criterion is this sentence serving. The student sees the comment attached to her own words, in her own document, and has to resolve it herself. That is a far sharper teaching instrument than a verbal remark about the section as a whole.

The criteria reward focus and method, subject knowledge, critical thinking, presentation and the quality of the student's reflection. Written comments map onto those cleanly because each comment can be tagged with the criterion it concerns. By the third draft a student can usually predict the comment before it arrives, which is the point at which she has internalised the standard and the tutoring has done its job. An Extended Essay (EE) tutor in Mumbai working this way is training a reader, not supplying a reader.

What the tutor does not do is resolve any comment himself. Suggestion mode stays off. No tracked change is ever proposed by him, because an accepted suggestion is text the student did not write. If a sentence is beyond saving, the comment says so and says why, and the student writes a new one. Three drafts of her own prose beats one draft of somebody else's, and only one of those is hers to sign.

sections.heading: Which Mumbai zones gain most from online EE sessions?
paragraphs: An IB DP extended essay online tutor in Mumbai removes a travel problem that varies enormously by zone, so the gain is not evenly spread. In South Mumbai the distances are short and the evenings are slow: a tutor moving from Parel or Sewri down to Colaba or Walkeshwar loses time to signals rather than to kilometres, and the Coastal Road has changed some of those runs but not the Peddar Road ones. Island families often still prefer home classes and use online only for the between-session marking.

The Western Suburbs are where online earns its keep on a weekday. A specialist living in Vile Parle cannot hold a 6pm slot in Borivali or Dahisar twice a week, whatever he says in September, because the Western Express Highway will not let him. Students in Oshiwara, Versova, Jogeshwari, Malad West and Kandivali get a better tutor online than they get in person, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 only partly fix that. In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali have no station of their own and are reached off the JVLR from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, so a Powai student with a 9pm study habit is far better served remotely; Kurla and Mulund sit on the Central Line and have more in-person choice.

The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Mankhurd and Bhandup to Mulund, with the Eastern Freeway and the Monorail to Wadala making the island closer than it looks, and the SCLR linking across to Santacruz. Even so, a Govandi or Bhandup family looking for a Film or Global Politics specialist will not find one within half an hour. Navi Mumbai spreads across Airoli, Ghansoli, Vashi, Nerul, Seawoods, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel on Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and while the Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line have shortened the crossing, no tutor crosses the creek twice a week for a year. Thane stretches from the station through Majiwada and Hiranandani Estate out along Pokhran Road and Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali, where the evening crawl on Ghodbunder is reason enough on its own.

So the practical rule we give families is geographic. Inside South Mumbai and along the Central Line, in-person is realistic and online is an accelerant. In Kasarvadavali, Panvel, Dahisar and Bhandup, online is the only way to reach a scarce specialist weekly for a year, and home tuition is the thing you add for the occasional long session rather than the default.

Western Suburbs: Oshiwara, Versova, Malad West, Borivali, Dahisar

Navi Mumbai: Airoli, Ghansoli, Seawoods, Kharghar, Panvel, node to node

sections.heading: Mumbai school calendars and the long-project failure mode
paragraphs: Every Mumbai IB school sets internal Extended Essay milestones inside the IB's outer deadline, and the internal ones are what your household lives by. The recognisable shape is a subject and draft question late in DP1, a first full draft around the DP1 to DP2 transition, and submission in DP2 while Internal Assessments and mock examinations are also live. Your DP coordinator publishes the actual dates. Ask for them in writing and build the term from them rather than from an assumption.

Families we work with attend Jamnabai Narsee International School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School in Juhu, Ascend International School in Bandra Kurla Complex, JBCN International School, Parel and JBCN International School, Borivali, Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East, Podar International School in Santacruz and Powai, Witty International School in Malad and Chembur, Ryan Global School in Kandivali and Worli, Activity High School on Peddar Road, Gopi Birla Memorial School in Walkeshwar, Oberoi International School, JVLR, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai. Naming a school is local context only. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named here, and not affiliated with the International Baccalaureate organisation.

The failure mode on this particular assessment is not difficulty. It is dormancy. Between the day a question is approved and the day a draft is due there may be three months with nothing enforceable in them, and a seventeen-year-old with Internal Assessments due next week will rationally spend those three months on the Internal Assessments. The essay then restarts from a cold standstill in the worst possible fortnight. This is the single most common story we hear in Mumbai, and it is the reason a short weekly online check-in beats a long monthly one.

Two periods deserve a note in the diary. The monsoon stretch from June to September cancels in-person sessions and quietly ends projects that had no online fallback, which is a reason to run at least part of the term remotely from the start. And the Diwali to December window in DP2 is when the essay, the TOK essay and university applications land together, so anything not finished by then will be finished badly.

sections.heading: Online, home tuition or hybrid for a year-long essay?
paragraphs: Online is the lead mode on this page because the work genuinely fits it, and we will say where it does not. An IB DP extended essay online tutor in Mumbai gives you subject match over postcode match, short sessions that are not worth a commute, asynchronous marking that costs no travel, and a written record of every comment made on the essay, which is a useful thing to have if a question about authorship ever arises. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can also be swapped at short notice without the travel renegotiation that an in-person match needs.

Home tuition is still the better choice for some students and we match it on the same platform. A student who will not open the document unless somebody is physically present needs home classes, not a video call. So does a student who has lost confidence and is hiding the state of her reading, because that is visible across a table and concealable on a screen. Families who search for IB home tuition in Mumbai after two months of unproductive calls are usually right to switch, and an IB home tutor in Mumbai is often the correct answer for the first month and the wrong answer for the last.

Hybrid is what most of our Extended Essay families end up with, and the split is usually functional rather than alternating. The live screen-shared hour handles searching, sources and the hard conversation about scope. A home session once or twice a term handles the long drafting review where a table full of printouts helps. The between-session marking is always remote, because it should be. Extended Essay (EE) home classes Mumbai tutors travel to and the online check-ins are not competing: they do different jobs.

The honest trade-off against online is attention. A fifteen-year-old alone in a bedroom on a video call can drift, and a tutor cannot see the phone on her lap. We handle it with structure rather than surveillance: cameras on, the student shares her screen rather than the tutor sharing his, she drives every search and every edit, and the session ends with her typing the next week's task into the document herself. If that structure is not holding by week four, the match should move to home tuition and we will say so.

sections.heading: How are online EE tutors in Mumbai checked, and what should you check?
paragraphs: Three checks happen before a tutor reaches a shortlist: identity, the subject credential at the level the essay needs, and evidence that he has supervised or assessed research rather than only taught a syllabus. For remote work we add a fourth, which is the workflow. An IB DP extended essay online tutor in Mumbai has to describe, before he is listed, how he handles a shared document: where his comments go, what he does when a paragraph is unsalvageable, and why suggestion mode stays off. A vague answer there ends the application.

We also ask every tutor to state the boundary in his own words. The permitted work is teaching skills, questioning a draft the student wrote, and marking it against the published criteria. The excluded work is writing, redrafting, researching, supplying sources or reference lists, and producing any part of the essay. A tutor who hears that and starts negotiating about how much editing is really editing is not listed, because on this assessment that negotiation is the whole risk.

Your own checks take one conversation and a look at the document. Ask the tutor which subject he studied and to what level. Ask him to screen-share his own comment style on a sample paragraph so you can see whether he asks or tells. Then open your child's document yourself, look at the revision history, and check that every change is in her name. That last step takes a minute and it is the only verification that cannot be talked around. Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, and be wary of anyone whose comments contain replacement sentences. IB Gram does not guarantee grades.

Keep a light record at home. Note which days drafts went in and which days comments came back, and at four weeks ask your child one question: are you doing more of this yourself than you were in week one? On an online match that is the measure that matters, because the convenience of remote working is exactly what makes the lazy version of it easy to slide into.

sections.heading: Working in a shared document without a tutor ever typing in it
paragraphs: Here is the mechanic in full, because it is what you are actually buying. The student owns the document. She shares it with comment access only, not edit access, which means the permission system enforces the boundary rather than the tutor's self-discipline. His comments attach to her sentences. Each one is a question or a judgement: this claim is broader than your evidence, this paragraph serves no criterion, you have cited this source twice for two different points and only one of them is in it. She resolves each comment by rewriting, and the resolved thread stays in the history as a record of who said what.

The marking happens between sessions, which is the second half of the design. A student submits a section by Sunday night. The tutor reads it on Monday and returns comments by Tuesday, with a short written summary naming the two things to fix and the one thing to keep. Thursday's live hour then starts from marked work, and the whole hour goes on thinking: why is this question not answerable with these sources, what would change if you dropped the third case, how would you defend this to your supervisor. Reading a draft aloud in a paid hour is a waste of the hour.

Screen-sharing a search is the part students remember. The tutor does not share his screen and produce results. The student shares hers and searches, badly at first, while he watches and narrates what she is doing: you have used a phrase where a subject term would work better, you have not restricted the date range, this database has a thesaurus you have never opened, that result is a review rather than a study. She repeats the search until it works. She keeps the skill. If he searched for her, she would keep a list of links and learn nothing, and the sources would not be hers to claim.

Then there is cadence, which is unglamorous and decides the outcome. A year-long project needs small, frequent commitments rather than large rare ones. We schedule a twenty to twenty-five minute check-in on a fixed weekday for the weeks between full sessions: what did you search, what went in the log, what is next, done. It is cheap, it is short enough that no one cancels it, and it is the single most effective thing on this page, because the essays that fail in Mumbai are rarely the ones that were hard. They are the ones that went quiet in August. A home tutor for Extended Essay (EE) Mumbai families book for drafting weeks is a good addition to that cadence, not a replacement for it.
