sections.heading: Why the first term of DP1 decides so much for Mumbai beginners
paragraphs: Every other Diploma subject gives a student somewhere to stand. A DP1 student who loses a fortnight of Economics can still reason about a demand curve from general knowledge and common sense. A beginner in French who loses a fortnight has nothing underneath: the structures introduced in those two weeks are the ones the next unit assumes, and there is no earlier year of the language to fall back on. That asymmetry is the whole argument for starting a tutor in the first term instead of waiting for a mark that confirms what you already suspected in September.

In practice, the first term has to deliver four things. The sound-to-spelling mapping, so the student can hear a word and write a plausible version of it and see a word and say a plausible version of it. A small set of high-frequency verbs in the present, used so often they stop requiring thought. The habit of writing a short piece in French every few days rather than only when something is due. And enough listening that an unfamiliar voice is not alarming. None of those four is glamorous, all four are testable, and a tutor who can show you progress on them in October is giving you a far better signal than one reporting that sessions are going well.

The second thing families misjudge is how quietly a beginner language decays. In DP2 the EE deadline, the TOK essay and two or three IAs all land in the same stretch, and French is the subject with nothing due tomorrow, so it is the one that gets dropped from the evening without anyone deciding to drop it. Three weeks later the student sits a listening paper and does badly, and the conclusion drawn at home is that they are bad at languages. They are not. They stopped doing twenty minutes a day. A weekly tutor whose first question is whether the daily practice happened is doing the most valuable part of the job.

The third is expectation. A true beginner who works steadily for two years can reach a genuinely useful standard of everyday French, and that is worth saying because the course is often spoken about in Mumbai as either trivially easy or impossibly hard. It is neither. What it does not survive is a late start combined with irregular practice, and what it rewards is unglamorous consistency from September of DP1. If a family is deciding in June whether to add tuition from the beginning, the honest advice is that an early term of light, regular support costs less than a rescue in February and works better. An IB DP French ab initio tutor in Mumbai booked for weekly home tuition in August is doing cheaper and more effective work than the same tutor booked after the first mock.

sections.heading: Progress for a beginner at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: Four weeks in, the honest markers are mechanical and easy to check at the dining table. The student should be able to read a short unfamiliar French sentence aloud without freezing, write a few sentences about themselves without looking anything up, and recognise the core verbs when they hear them. They should also be able to tell you what the current theme is and what they are meant to be practising daily. No grade will have moved in four weeks, and a tutor claiming otherwise is reading noise. What should have changed is the student's relationship with the subject: less flinching, more attempting.

By the end of a term the test is accuracy on things already covered. Spelling attempts should be plausible rather than random. Short written pieces should be dull but correct, with verbs in the right place. Listening to a familiar theme at normal speed should produce most of the gist rather than panic. A student who has stopped making three different kinds of error has improved even if the mark has not caught up yet, which happens often and is not a failure. Ask the tutor for the marked work and compare where the losses sit now against where they sat in the first month.

Across the full cycle to the May session the honest framing is that a tutor shifts probability. Two years of a held weekly hour with daily practice behind it puts a beginner in the strongest position the available hours allow. It cannot undo a start made in DP2, it cannot replace the student's own daily contact with the language, and it cannot control an off day in a recorded oral. Beginners also plateau, usually somewhere in the middle of DP2, and most of them move again once rehearsal and revision become systematic rather than occasional.

If four to six weeks of genuinely attended sessions have produced nothing on those mechanical markers, treat it as information. Sometimes the tutor is too gentle, sometimes too fast, sometimes the student needs someone who will make them write the same paragraph four times. Tell us what is not working and a new shortlist comes back through the same checks. Changing tutor once over two years is normal. Changing monthly usually means the problem is daily practice rather than teaching, and we would rather say that than keep sending profiles.

sections.heading: Booking a French ab initio home tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Gather three things before the first session and that hour becomes genuinely diagnostic. Whatever French material the school has issued so far, including the theme list and any vocabulary sheets, because a tutor who knows the school's sequence can align to it instead of running a parallel course. Any marked French work, even a short class exercise, since a single piece of writing tells a teacher more than a conversation with a parent does. And the honest picture of the week: school hours, travel, activities, the two Higher Level subjects and the realistic window for daily practice.

Expect the first session to look like testing rather than teaching, and do not be alarmed by that. A good beginner diagnostic reads a few words aloud to check the sound-to-spelling mapping, dictates a short phrase to see what the student writes, asks for a few sentences in writing, plays a short listening clip at full speed, and asks the student to say three things about themselves in French. By the end the tutor should name the weakest of those four and say exactly what the first month will target and what the student owes between sessions.

After that, the whole thing comes down to protecting the routine. Fix a slot you can defend against everything but illness. Keep every piece of marked work in one folder so the pattern is visible in February rather than guessed at. When EE or IA weeks arrive, tell the tutor so the French hour becomes lighter instead of being cancelled, because a cancelled week in a beginner language costs more than a cancelled week in History does. And keep the daily twenty minutes going even in those weeks, in whatever reduced form survives.

One boundary, stated plainly because parents find it awkward to raise. The tutor may teach, drill, model, question and mark. The tutor may not write, part-write or supply any portion of a piece the student submits, and a good tutor will say no if asked. For a beginner this matters more than it sounds, because the gap between what the student can produce alone and what a fluent adult would produce is wide and obvious to an examiner. The work has to be the student's own.

faqs.question: My child has never studied French. Is ab initio realistic in two years?
faqs.answer: Yes, with regular work, and that qualification is the whole answer. French ab initio is designed for genuine beginners and takes them to everyday communication on a set of defined themes across Diploma Programme Years 1 and 2. What makes it realistic is frequency rather than intensity: twenty minutes of daily contact plus a weekly taught hour from the first term of DP1 gets a beginner a long way. What makes it unrealistic is starting the real work in DP2, when the Extended Essay and Internal Assessments are already occupying every evening and the language has nothing earlier to fall back on.

faqs.question: Is French ab initio an easier way to a high grade?
faqs.answer: No, and the assumption causes real damage. The vocabulary list is smaller than French B's, which is why the course looks soft from outside, but the student is building a language from zero in the same two years that carry five other subjects, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. The grade depends on accuracy under timed conditions in writing, listening, reading and speech, none of which a beginner has a reserve of. Choose it because the student is a beginner, which is what it is for, not because it looks like a shortcut.

faqs.question: My child already knows some French. Can we still choose ab initio?
faqs.answer: That is the school's decision, taken with you, and the usual answer for a student with real prior French is no. Ab initio is built for beginners, and a student with several years of French behind them is both wrongly placed and likely to be moved once the school reviews prior learning. If you believe the record misstates what your child has actually studied, write to the languages coordinator early in DP1 and set out the prior learning plainly. Leaving it until marks exist makes the conversation harder and the options narrower.

faqs.question: Can a beginner French tutor travel to Airoli or Sanpada for an evening slot?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if the tutor is based in a neighbouring Navi Mumbai node rather than across the creek. Airoli and Sanpada sit on the Trans-Harbour and Harbour lines with Palm Beach Road and the Thane-Belapur stretch behind them, so a tutor from Vashi, Ghansoli or Nerul can hold a weekday evening hour for a full term. A tutor coming from Bandra or Dadar for the same slot will ask to change the day by November, whatever they say in August. Ab initio teachers are a thin pool across Navi Mumbai, so ask about home tuition and online options together before ruling either out.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor from the first week of DP1, or can we wait?
faqs.answer: Earlier is cheaper and works better for this specific course. A beginner language has no earlier year to absorb a missed fortnight, so a gap that appears in September is still a gap in January unless someone fills it. Light, regular support from the first term usually costs less overall than a rescue arrangement in February, and it is far less unpleasant for the student. If you are deciding in June, the reasonable position is to start with one modest weekly home tuition slot and scale it to what the first assessments actually show. Most families who book an IB DP French ab initio tutor in Mumbai in the first term never need to escalate to anything heavier.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a beginner French tutor?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not invent a price list. Scarcity matters most here, because tutors with specific ab initio experience are a smaller pool than French B or Maths tutors. Then travel distance and the time the commute costs the tutor; session length and weekly frequency; whether sessions are at your home or online; and the stage of the course, since a DP2 rescue typically needs more hours per week than a steady DP1 build. Ask for the per-session rate and the expected number of sessions in writing before you commit to a term.

faqs.question: How does gate access work when a home tutor visits our society in Thane?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a standing weekly visitor and it stops being an issue. Most Thane complexes along Pokhran Road, Kolshet and Hiranandani Estate run an app-based or register-based visitor system, and a recurring entry saves the tutor ten minutes at the gate every week. Tell us the protocol when you book, including whether the tutor needs a resident to approve entry each time, and whether parking is available or the tutor should come by autorickshaw. Small logistics are what quietly break a 7pm slot on Ghodbunder Road in the monsoon.

faqs.question: My child can say sentences but cannot spell anything. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Very normal at the start, and it is the first thing a tutor should fix. French maps sounds to letters consistently, but not in ways obvious to a reader of English, Hindi or Marathi, so a beginner who has learned orally will speak ahead of what they can write. Deliberate work on that mapping, dictation of short phrases and reading aloud from text, closes the gap within a few weeks if it is done early. Left alone until the first written assessment, it turns into lost marks that look like carelessness but are structural.

faqs.question: How much practice does a beginner need between sessions?
faqs.answer: Twenty minutes a day beats two hours on a Sunday, and that is not a slogan about discipline. Vocabulary recall, spelling and listening all respond to frequency: five short contacts a week embed what one long session does not. The practical version is ten minutes of vocabulary or spelling and ten minutes of listening to something in French, every weekday. Protect it in Extended Essay weeks in whatever reduced form survives, because the weeks a student stops entirely are the weeks the decay happens, and the recovery costs more than the practice would have.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a complete beginner?
faqs.answer: It works, with one real limitation. Listening drills, vocabulary recall, spelling checks and marked work all transfer well to a screen, and for families in Ulwe, Panvel or Kasarvadavali an online tutor may simply be a better ab initio teacher than anyone within a sensible drive. The limitation is pronunciation correction and the tutor's read on attention, both of which are weaker through a camera in the first term when habits are forming. Many beginner families run weekly home classes for speech and writing plus short online slots for drills.

faqs.question: What if there is no progress after four weeks?
faqs.answer: Check the mechanical markers first, then act. Can the student read a short unfamiliar sentence aloud, write a few sentences unaided, and name the current theme and daily task? If not, ask the tutor which of those they are targeting and how, and whether the daily practice is actually happening, since four half-done weeks are not four weeks of tuition. If the answers are vague, that is the diagnosis. Tell us and a different shortlist comes back under the same identity, qualification and beginner-experience checks, usually avoiding whatever attribute failed.

faqs.question: The tutor is a native speaker but has not taught the IB. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, for this course it matters a great deal. Speaking French fluently and teaching an absolute beginner towards a defined assessment are different skills, and the second one depends on sequencing: what to introduce first, how much English to use in week two, which errors to correct now and which to leave. We record ab initio teaching experience separately from general French competence for exactly that reason. Any variety of French is fine as a model, whether the tutor learned in Pune, Paris, Brussels, Dakar or Montreal; what we check is whether they have taught beginners through both Diploma years.

We filter for tutors who have taught ab initio across both Diploma years, send two or three verified profiles, and set up a diagnostic first session at home or online. After it you keep the tutor, ask for a different profile, or stop there. Starting in the first term is the single best decision available.

sections.heading: How IB Gram turns a French B home tuition request in Mumbai into a shortlist
paragraphs: A French B request is never generic. The parent who writes in usually has something specific on the table: a Paper 2 mock where the reading answers sounded plausible but were not actually drawn from the passage, a listening section that ran out before the last items were attempted, or a written task that was warm and fluent and still scored poorly because a letter had been written as an essay. International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) French B rewards doing the right thing with the text in front of you. That is a trainable habit rather than a gift, so the first thing we ask for is evidence rather than a wish list.

Evidence means the last marked script, the teacher's written comments, and the student's own account of where the minutes went. Those three things narrow a shortlist faster than any questionnaire. A student whose comprehension collapses only on the longer text needs a different tutor from one whose accuracy falls apart under timed conditions. When a family asks for IB DP French B home tuition in Mumbai, the match is made on which component is losing marks, which level the student sits, and which corridor the household is in, because a tutor who cannot reach you reliably at seven in the evening is not a match however strong the subject knowledge.

The shortlist is small on purpose. Two or three profiles, each of whom has taken French B students through to final examinations, is more useful than a long list of availability. Speak to each one about technique. Ask how they would handle a reading answer that paraphrases the passage badly, or what they do in the first ten minutes of a listening lesson. The answers separate candidates quickly. There is no single best IB tutor in Mumbai for French B, because the right tutor depends entirely on which paper is the problem and how your household's week is already built.

Searches like IB tutors near me Mumbai return a great deal of general language tuition, and French B is not general language tuition. It is assessed against published criteria by examiners looking for specific behaviours, so a teacher who has only ever taught conversational French will coach the language well and the examination badly. Ask directly whether the tutor has marked work against the French B criteria and whether they can show you, on your child's own script, how a band was reached.

sections.heading: Where French B sits in the Diploma Programme, and why that shapes practice
paragraphs: French B is a language acquisition course in the IB Diploma Programme, taken by students who already have some French behind them from the Middle Years Programme (MYP), from IGCSE, or from years of school French elsewhere. It runs at Higher Level (HL) and at Standard Level (SL), and which level and which language a student takes is a placement decision made by the school together with the family. This page does not try to influence that choice. It assumes the choice is made and asks a narrower question: given that your child is sitting French B, what does good examination preparation look like?

The answer starts with the shape of the course. French B is organised around prescribed themes rather than around a list of grammar points, and the themes recur across reading texts, listening audio, written tasks and the oral. A student who treats the themes as the organising structure builds vocabulary that transfers between components. A student who treats French B as a grammar syllabus with some topics attached ends up with accurate sentences and nothing to say. A good French B tutor in Mumbai works thematically and brings grammar in where a theme demands it.

Assessment splits into externally marked papers and an internally assessed oral. HL and SL face components of the same broad shape at different levels of demand, with HL carrying a literary element that SL does not. The specifics of structure, timing and weighting are revised by the IB on its own cycle, so do not take any figure from a tutor, an agency, or this page. Read the current subject guide, or ask your child's DP coordinator, and plan from that.

What stays constant is the behaviour being rewarded. Across every component, French B asks the student to understand a source accurately, respond to a task as it was set, and control language well enough that meaning is never in doubt. Everything in the rest of this page is a method for drilling one of those three things.

sections.heading: Paper by paper: what each French B component is really testing
paragraphs: The reading section is not a general knowledge test, and this is where the largest avoidable losses happen. A student reads a text about urban cycling in Lyon, recognises the topic, and answers from what she knows about urban cycling rather than from what this writer said about it. The answer is sensible, well expressed, and wrong, because the mark is for retrieving the writer's point. The drill is mechanical and it works: before writing anything, underline the words in the passage that carry the answer, then write the answer so that it could be traced straight back to those words. A tutor who marks reading work should be asking, every single time, where in the text that came from.

Listening is a timing problem as much as a comprehension problem. Replay is limited, the audio moves at its own pace, and a student who stops to perfect item four loses items nine and ten. The habit to build is reading the questions in the gap before the audio starts so the ear knows what it is hunting for, writing partial answers rather than nothing, and moving on without arguing with the recording. French-speaking cultures are plural, and the audio reflects that: a speaker from Dakar, Brussels, Geneva, Montreal, Casablanca or Abidjan sounds different from a Parisian newsreader, and all of those varieties are proper French. Students whose only input has been one accent get a shock. Students in Mumbai households that already switch between Marathi, Hindi, Gujarati, English and more usually adapt faster than they expect, because the ear is already trained to retune.

The written task is where fluent students are most often surprised. The task names a text type and an audience, and a blog post, an email to a host family, a report for a school magazine and a speech each carry conventions that a marker is looking for. Register is part of the assessment, not decoration on top of it. A student who writes an elegant essay when the task asked for a leaflet has lost marks that no amount of accurate subjunctive will recover. The oral, meanwhile, rewards the student who can keep talking usefully under a follow-up question rather than the student who has memorised a monologue.

sections.heading: Which parts of Mumbai do French B home tutors cover?
paragraphs: French B home tuition is available across all six Mumbai zones, but the practical limit is travel time at the hour you actually want the lesson. In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clock is not: a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba or Cuffe Parade covers a few kilometres and can still lose forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. Families in Walkeshwar, Fort and Tardeo are usually matched inside the island rather than waiting for someone to come down the Western Line. Metro Line 3 and the Coastal Road have changed some of these runs, but the evening peak still decides the slot.

The Western Suburbs are the densest band of French B demand in the city, and they run north to south along the Western Express Highway, the Link Road and the Western Line. Matching along the line works; matching across it does not. A tutor based in Khar West will hold a standing slot in Santacruz West, Bandra or Juhu for two years. The same tutor asked to reach Malad, Kandivali or Borivali at 6pm will cancel by the third week. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the Dahisar to Andheri stretch workable in a way the highway alone never was, so Goregaon East and Andheri West pairings are more reliable than they used to be.

The Central Suburbs centre on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR. Powai is the exception in Mumbai, Maharashtra: physically central, with no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg, Kurla or Ghatkopar. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund, and the Eastern Freeway makes Wadala and Chembur far closer to the island than the map suggests. In Navi Mumbai, matching is node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel sit minutes apart on Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and the Atal Setu has shortened the crossing without making a weekday island-to-Kharghar run sensible. Thane runs west to east from the station across Pokhran Road and Majiwada, and Ghodbunder Road sets the timetable: near the station to Kasarvadavali is twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour by evening.

sections.heading: How the Mumbai school calendar decides when exam technique gets drilled
paragraphs: Mumbai families sitting French B are mostly at schools whose calendars pile internal assessment, mock examinations and coursework deadlines into the same narrow windows. Students at Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai and Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane all deal with the same shape of year even where the detail differs. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, or with any language-certification body. The schools are named because their calendars are the pressure your tutor has to plan around.

The useful consequence is that exam technique has to be drilled when there is room for it, not when it becomes urgent. The quiet stretch early in DP1 is when a student can afford to spend a whole hour on a single reading passage, working out where every answer came from. By the time DP2 mocks arrive, there is no room for that kind of slow work, because the Extended Essay (EE), the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay and three or four Internal Assessment (IA) deadlines are competing for the same evenings.

The monsoon matters more than parents expect. A tutor who commits to a Thane or Powai evening slot in a dry November is making a promise they may not keep in July, when Ghodbunder Road and the Eastern Express Highway behave very differently. Agree a monsoon fallback at the start: same time, same day, online, no renegotiation. It keeps the sequence of lessons intact in the months when continuity matters most.

Mock season is also when a French B tutor earns their place. The student comes home with a marked script and a mark that feels unfair. The tutor's job is to go through it line by line, identify which of the three behaviours failed, and convert the disappointment into a list of two or three repeatable fixes. A tutor who responds to a bad mock with reassurance rather than a list of fixes is not helping.

sections.heading: Is home tuition, online or hybrid better for French B exam technique?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the lead option and the one most Mumbai families choose, because exam technique work is physical. There are marked scripts on the table, a highlighter, a printed passage with the answer sources underlined, and a criteria sheet the student is annotating. A tutor sitting next to a student can see the moment her eye leaves the passage and starts answering from memory, and can stop it there. That intervention is much harder to make over a screen. IB DP French B home tuition in Mumbai also removes the travel burden from the student, which matters when the alternative is an hour on the Western Express Highway after a full school day.

Online is genuinely good for two things and weak at a third. It is excellent for listening practice, because the audio reaches the student at full quality through headphones rather than through a laptop speaker in a room with a mixer running. It is excellent for oral rehearsal, where frequent short sessions beat one long weekly one, and a fifteen minute call three times a week is only possible without travel. It is weaker for the marking conversation, where two people need to be looking at the same piece of paper. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can run the first two well and should be honest about the third.

Hybrid is what most French B students end up on by DP2, and it is a deliberate structure rather than a compromise. One home session a week for the marking conversation and the written task work, plus two short online calls for listening and oral drilling. Whether you call it an IB private tutor Mumbai arrangement or home tuition, the format is one to one, and the question is only which part of the week happens in your living room. Families in Kharghar, Panvel and Kasarvadavali lean harder on the online half for the simple reason that the evening road does not cooperate.

sections.heading: How are French B home tutors in Mumbai checked, and what should you check?
paragraphs: Every tutor listed for IB DP French B home tuition in Mumbai has had their identity documents and their claimed teaching history checked before a profile goes live, and anything we could not verify is not on the profile. Subject claims are checked separately from teaching claims, because they are different things: a tutor may have strong French and no experience of the French B criteria, and for this work the criteria experience is what you are buying. We ask for evidence of having taught the course through to final examinations rather than for a certificate.

What IB Gram cannot check for you is fit, and fit is most of the outcome. So there is a second layer of checking that belongs to you, and it takes one conversation. Ask the tutor to talk you through a band on the written task criteria in plain English. Ask what they would do with a student who writes beautifully and ignores the task. Ask how they handle a listening lesson when the student has already heard the audio once. A tutor who can answer those three questions concretely has done the work. A tutor who answers with a description of their own fluency has not.

Two things should make you stop. The first is a tutor who promises a specific grade. No honest tutor does that, because the student sits the paper and the examiner marks it, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades either. The second is any offer to help with a submission beyond teaching and marking. A tutor may teach a text type, explain a criterion and mark a draft with comments. A tutor may never write, redraft or supply any part of what your child submits, and a tutor who offers to is putting the student's academic honesty record at risk for a few marks.

Check the practical things too, before the first session rather than after. Confirm who is in the room, what the tutor expects the student to bring, and whether the written plan you were promised actually arrives.

sections.heading: Self-marking before the tutor marks: the habit that moves French B grades
paragraphs: The single most useful change a French B student can make is to mark her own written task against the published criteria before she hands it to anyone. Not read it over. Mark it, with the criteria sheet open, awarding herself a band for each strand and writing one sentence of justification for each. It feels artificial for the first three attempts and then it starts to work, because the student stops writing for a vague sense of quality and starts writing for the thing that is actually assessed. By the fifth attempt she is catching the register mismatch herself, which is the point.

Self-marking only works against the real criteria, so get them from the school or the current subject guide rather than from a summary someone has retyped. The student then hands over both the task and her own marking. The tutor marks independently and the two sets of judgements are compared. Where they agree, the student has internalised that strand. Where they differ, there is a specific, teachable gap, and the conversation is about why the tutor read it differently rather than about whether the piece was good.

Planning sits upstream of all of this. Most written task marks are lost before the first sentence, when a student reads the task, spots a familiar topic, and starts writing. Three minutes of planning fixes it: name the text type, name the audience, decide the register, list three points, then write. That plan is also what makes writing to the task possible instead of writing to length. Students pad because they have run out of plan, and padding costs marks twice, once for irrelevance and once for the errors that creep in when a student writes sentences she does not need.

The last piece is the student's own error list, kept in a notebook and nowhere else. Not a general list of French difficulties. Her list: the agreement she gets wrong, the preposition she guesses, the tense she avoids by rephrasing. Six or seven recurring errors, drilled deliberately, will move a script further than another twenty vocabulary items. A good tutor builds that list from the student's marked work over a few weeks and then refuses to let her leave a session without correcting two of them. French B home classes Mumbai students attend after school are at their most valuable when fifteen minutes of every hour goes to that list.

sections.heading: What progress in French B honestly looks like at four weeks and one term
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking for a grade change, and a tutor who points at one is reading noise. What you should see is behavioural: the student underlining the passage before answering, producing a three-line plan before a written task, and being able to tell you which band her last piece hit and why. If those three things are not happening after four sessions, the sessions are being spent on content rather than on technique, and that is a conversation to have immediately rather than at the end of term.

At one term the marks start to follow, and they follow unevenly. Reading usually moves first, because the fix is procedural and the student either traces her answers to the text or she does not. Listening moves next, over perhaps two months, as the pre-reading and partial-answer habits bed in. Writing moves slowest, because register and text type control are judgement rather than procedure, and judgement takes a dozen marked pieces. A home tutor for French B Mumbai families book in DP1 has time for that dozen. One engaged in February of DP2 does not, and should say so.

By one full examination cycle the honest claim is narrower than most marketing suggests: a student who has drilled technique consistently will convert the French she already has into marks much more reliably than a student who has not. That is worth real points. It is not a promise about an outcome. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and neither should anyone you speak to, because the examiner marks the script and nobody in your living room controls that.

The failure mode worth naming is the comfortable plateau. A student who is reasonably good at French can coast on existing ability, produce consistently acceptable work, and stop improving entirely, because nothing in the weekly session is hard enough to force a change. If the tutor's marking comments have stopped changing from week to week, the work has got too easy. Ask for harder texts, tighter timing, and an unseen task with no preparation.

sections.heading: Starting IB DP French B home tuition in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Three documents make the first session useful instead of exploratory. The most recent marked French B script, whatever state it is in. The teacher's comments, even if they are two lines. And the current criteria for whichever component is the problem, taken from the school or the subject guide. With those on the table, a tutor can diagnose in one session what would otherwise take three. Without them, the first hour goes on finding out what the examiner already told you.

The first session should be narrow. One component, one timed piece done in front of the tutor, then the student self-marking it while the tutor marks it separately. Comparing the two is the diagnosis. By the end you should have a written plan naming which component gets attention for the next six weeks, which two habits are being built, and what the student brings each week. If the session ends with a general assessment of ability and no plan, ask for the plan.

Set the practical terms in the same conversation. The day and time, the fallback for monsoon weeks and school trips, who is home during the session, and where in the flat the work happens, which should be a table rather than a bedroom. Settle how cancellations work on both sides before you need to use it. IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on level, on how scarce the subject is, on how far the tutor travels and on session length, so ask for the structure in writing rather than a number over the phone.

One last thing to agree out loud, with the student in the room: the tutor teaches and marks, and the student writes. Every word submitted is hers. A French B IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai families keep for both years is worth far more than a short, intense rescue, so set that boundary early and it never becomes a question later.

faqs.question: What does IB DP French B home tuition in Mumbai actually cover in the first session?
faqs.answer: One component, diagnosed properly, rather than a tour of the whole course. A good first session has the student produce a short timed piece on the paper that is losing marks, then mark it herself against the criteria while the tutor marks it separately. Comparing the two judgements shows exactly where her reading of her own work differs from an examiner's. The session should end with a written plan naming the component, the two habits being built, and what she brings next week. IB DP French B home tuition in Mumbai that begins with a general chat about ability has wasted an hour.

faqs.question: My daughter answers reading questions from general knowledge. How is that fixed?
faqs.answer: Mechanically, and faster than you would expect. The rule is that nothing goes on the answer line until the words carrying it have been underlined in the passage. For the first two weeks the tutor asks, on every answer, where in the text that came from, and the student has to point. It feels tedious and it retrains the reflex. Within about a month the underlining happens automatically and the general-knowledge answers stop appearing. This is the highest-yield fix in French B reading because the loss is pure technique, not comprehension: she understood the passage perfectly well and answered a different question.

faqs.question: The listening section is where he loses most marks. Can that genuinely be trained?
faqs.answer: Yes, because most listening losses are timing and strategy rather than ear. Three habits do the work: read the questions in the gap before the audio starts so the ear knows its targets, write a partial answer instead of a blank whenever anything was caught, and move on without arguing with the recording when an item is gone. Replay is limited, so a student who stays with one item loses three later ones. Practice also needs plural accents, because French is spoken across Senegal, Belgium, Switzerland, Quebec, Morocco, Haiti and more, and a student fed only one accent is unprepared.

faqs.question: Her written task was fluent and well expressed but scored badly. Why would that happen?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the text type and register did not match the task. A written task names a form and an audience, and a blog post, an email to a host family, a report and a speech each carry conventions a marker is looking for. A student who writes an elegant essay when the task asked for a leaflet loses marks that accurate grammar cannot recover. The fix is three minutes of planning before writing: name the text type, name the audience, fix the register, list three points. Then write to the task rather than to length, because padding costs marks for irrelevance and for the errors padding introduces.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Cuffe Parade for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor is matched inside South Mumbai rather than brought down from the suburbs. Distances on the island are short but the evening peak at Peddar Road and Haji Ali is slow, so a Worli to Cuffe Parade run that looks like fifteen minutes can take forty. Tutors living in Walkeshwar, Tardeo, Worli or Fort hold Cuffe Parade and Colaba slots reliably for two years. A tutor commuting from Andheri or Thane for a 7pm island slot will manage it for a month and then start rescheduling, which is worse for continuity than a slightly different tutor.

faqs.question: What happens at our society gate and building reception when a tutor first arrives?
faqs.answer: Tell us your building's policy when you book, because it decides what the tutor needs on day one. Most Mumbai societies want a photo ID at the gate, an entry in the visitor register, and a resident confirming the visit, either by app approval or a call from reception. Many complexes will issue a standing visitor pass once a weekly slot is established, which removes ten minutes of friction from every session. Tutors carry ID as standard. If your society requires police verification paperwork or a separate approval for repeat visitors, say so upfront and we will confirm the tutor can provide it.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a subject like French B?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not quote a figure because an invented price helps nobody. Level matters, since HL work takes longer to mark than SL. Subject scarcity matters, and French B specialists who have taken students through to examinations are thinner on the ground than Maths or Economics tutors. Travel distance matters, because a tutor crossing Mumbai in the evening peak is giving up more time than one walking across Khar West. Session length and frequency matter, as does whether part of the week runs online. Ask for the structure in writing before the first session.

faqs.question: Does online really work for French B, or is home tuition always better?
faqs.answer: Both, for different components, which is why most families end up hybrid. Home tuition is clearly better for the marking conversation and written task work, because two people need to be looking at the same annotated page and the tutor needs to see the student's eye leave the passage. Online is better for listening, where headphone audio beats a laptop speaker in a busy room, and for oral rehearsal, where three short calls a week beat one long session. A reasonable structure is one home session weekly plus two fifteen-minute online calls for listening and speaking.

faqs.question: It has been a month and I cannot see any improvement. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Check for habits rather than marks, because marks at four weeks are noise. Ask to see her last three pieces of work and look for three specific things: is the reading passage underlined before answers are written, is there a short plan above each written task, and can she tell you which band her last piece reached and why. If all three are present, the work is on track and the marks will follow over a term. If none are present, the sessions are being spent on content instead of technique. Raise it with the tutor directly, and if nothing changes within two sessions, ask us to rematch.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help write or tidy up her written task before she submits it?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach the text type, explain the criteria, and mark a draft with written comments the student then acts on herself. A tutor may never write, redraft, translate or supply any part of what your child submits. This is not a technicality we are being cautious about; it is an academic honesty boundary, and the consequences land on the student rather than the tutor. Say it out loud in the first session with the student present and it never becomes an awkward question in March. Any tutor who offers more than teaching and marking should be refused the slot.

faqs.question: Can you promise my son a specific French B grade by May?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who does is selling you something they cannot deliver. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, because your son sits the paper and an examiner marks it, and nobody in your living room controls either. What consistent technique work does reliably achieve is converting the French he already has into marks he was previously losing to procedure: answering from the text, finishing the listening section, matching text type to task. That is worth real points on a script. It is a different claim from a predicted number, and the difference matters when you are choosing between tutors.

sections.heading: How do you find an IB DP French B home tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: You start from the writing, because that is the part a parent can hand over. Send us one piece of your child's French writing, along with what text type it was supposed to be and what the brief asked her to do. An experienced French B teacher reads that in four minutes and can tell you whether the problem is the language, the convention, or the fact that nobody explained the difference between writing to a principal and writing to readers of a school blog.

An IB DP French B home tutor in Mumbai is being hired for a specific technical skill, which is marking. Most people who teach French in this city teach it well and have never marked against assessment criteria. The two jobs look similar from outside and are not. A tutor who can only tell your daughter that a sentence is wrong will fix her French slowly. A tutor who can tell her that the sentence is correct but the register is wrong for the audience named in the task is doing the thing that moves a written mark.

So the shortlist is built on component history: which text types she has set, whether she has prepared students for the individual oral at Standard Level, at Higher Level, or both, and whether she can show work she has marked with criteria referenced in the margin. Two or three profiles come back, each with a sentence explaining the fit. We tell you where the pool is thin, which in French B usually means the further you are from the Western Suburbs and South Mumbai, the more likely a hybrid arrangement makes sense.

The first home session is a working one. One task set under time, marked while your daughter watches, and an error list started on paper that stays in the house and gets added to every week. By the end of that session she should be able to name the three things costing her the most marks, and so should you. Nothing about that requires a contract first.
bullets: 1. Send one piece of writing and the text type it was meant to be.
2. Tell us the level and whether the individual oral has been recorded.
3. Two or three profiles arrive with marking and oral-preparation history.
4. First home session: one timed task, marked and annotated in front of her.
5. An error list goes on paper that session and stays in the house.

sections.heading: Where the assessed writing and the oral sit in French B
paragraphs: French B in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) is assessed through a Paper 1 writing task, a Paper 2 made of listening and reading, and an individual oral. Only two of those three are productive. Paper 2 asks the student to understand French. Paper 1 and the oral ask her to produce it, under time or under questioning, and they are where most of the recoverable marks on this course sit. A home tutor who spends every session on comprehension exercises is working on the half that is easier to teach and harder to improve.

Paper 1 is externally examined. The student receives a task, a text type, an audience and a purpose, and writes by hand. The individual oral is different in kind: it is conducted and assessed internally by the student's own teacher, recorded, and then moderated externally. That internal element is why the oral is the single most schedulable component in the Diploma. Everything else happens when the examination timetable says so. The oral happens when your school says so, which means it can be prepared for with a precise date in mind.

The stimulus differs by level. At Standard Level the oral is built on a visual stimulus linked to one of the course themes: the student is given an image, describes and interprets it in connection with that theme, and then holds a conversation about it. At Higher Level the current guide uses an extract from a literary work studied in class instead. Both then open into general conversation across the course. Confirm the arrangement for your child's cohort with the Diploma Programme coordinator, because the IB revises guides on its own cycle and a page on the internet is not the source of record.

A French B IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai parents engage should treat the oral as a DP1 project rather than a DP2 emergency. The skill it tests, speaking analytically about something unseen while somebody asks follow-up questions, takes months to build and about four days to fake. Families who start image work in the first year arrive at the recording with a student who can think out loud in French. Families who start six weeks out arrive with a student holding a script.
bullets: Paper 1 and the individual oral are the productive components.
Paper 1 is externally examined; the oral is internally assessed and moderated.
Standard Level orals use a visual stimulus linked to a course theme.
The Higher Level oral currently uses a literary extract instead.
The oral has a known date, so it can be planned backwards from.

sections.heading: Why is a blog post not the same task as a formal letter?
paragraphs: Because the reader is different, and in French B the reader is half the mark. Give a student the same content, a school trip to Lonavala, and ask for a blog post for her classmates and then a formal letter to the principal about the same trip, and almost nothing should survive the move except the facts. The blog opens with a title and a date, addresses the reader directly, uses tu or vous depending on who is being spoken to, asks a question or two, and invites comments. The letter opens with a formal salutation, holds vous without exception, uses impersonal and passive constructions, states its purpose in the first line and closes with a set formula.

An article is different again: a headline, an opening that makes the reader care, reported speech, statements attributed to people, a third-person stance even when the writer has an opinion. A speech is written to be heard, so it addresses an audience in the room, repeats for effect, asks rhetorical questions, and ends with something that works out loud. A report is organised under headings and prioritises clarity over style. A diary entry is dated, private, and in the first person. An interview alternates question and answer and keeps the two voices distinct.

Students lose marks here in predictable ways. They write a competent piece in no identifiable text type at all. They open a formal letter correctly and drift into tu by the third paragraph. They write a speech that reads like an essay, with no audience anywhere in it. They produce a blog post with no title, no date and no voice. The language in all four cases may be perfectly accurate. The convention marks go anyway, and the student usually has no idea why, because her teacher's comment said the French was good.

The discipline a home tutor should drill is reading the task before writing anything: who is the audience, what is the purpose, what text type is named, and what does that combination require in the first two lines and the last two. Two minutes spent on that before a pen moves is worth more than ten minutes of checking at the end. A good tutor will make your daughter annotate the task itself, in the margin, every single time, until she does it without being told.
bullets: Same content, different reader, almost nothing should carry across.
Formal letter: vous throughout, set opening and closing formulae.
Blog: title, date, direct address, a question, an invitation to respond.
Speech: an audience in the room, repetition, something that lands aloud.
Annotate audience, purpose and text type on the task before writing.

sections.heading: Home tuition for French B in every Mumbai zone
paragraphs: Navi Mumbai is the zone where the home-visit question gets decided fastest, so start there. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are planned nodes, a short drive apart along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 underneath. A French B tutor living in Nerul will happily cover Belapur and Vashi weekly. A French B tutor in Juhu will agree to Kharghar once, enjoy the Atal Setu, and start rescheduling by the fourth week. Node-to-node matching is not a limitation we apologise for. It is the only pattern that survives two years.

Thane behaves the same way with different roads. The city runs west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road out to Kasarvadavali, and Ghodbunder sets every schedule: twenty minutes off-peak, close to an hour in the evening. Thane tutors cover Thane, with occasional crossover from Mulund along the Eastern Express Highway. For families out near Kasarvadavali, a Saturday morning home session plus a short online midweek slot is usually more reliable than a weekday evening that depends on one road behaving.

In Mumbai, Maharashtra proper the pattern is corridor-based. The Western Suburbs hold the deepest French B pool: Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz West and Juhu form one cluster along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, Andheri West, Versova and Oshiwara another, and Malad, Kandivali East, Borivali and Dahisar a third, tied together by Metro Lines 2A and 7 and by Link Road. South Mumbai is short-distance and slow: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Worli, Babulnath and Tardeo, served by the Western and Harbour lines, Metro Line 3 and the Coastal Road, with the Bandra-Worli Sea Link bringing suburban tutors as far as Worli before the Peddar Road signals take back the time saved.

The Central Suburbs run on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR and no station of their own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar. Kurla and Ghatkopar are the easiest nodes to staff. In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund are covered by the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) bring in tutors from further away than the distance suggests. Wherever you are, settle the building access question before the first visit rather than during it.

sections.heading: Mumbai school deadlines that decide when the oral happens
paragraphs: Because the individual oral is internally assessed, your school fixes the recording window, and that single date reorganises everything else. Families at Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul are not all recording in the same month. Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for the window in the first term of DP2, or earlier if your school runs it early, and tell the tutor the moment you have it.

What that date does is convert vague oral preparation into a countable number of sessions. Eight weeks out, the student should be describing unfamiliar images aloud without notes. Four weeks out, she should be doing it with follow-up questions she has not heard before. Two weeks out, under something close to real conditions with a recording running, because hearing yourself back is uncomfortable and necessary. None of that works if the date arrives as a surprise in a corridor conversation.

The written side runs on a different clock. Mocks at most Mumbai IB schools fall in the early months of the calendar year, which is also when the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay and a cluster of Internal Assessment (IA) deadlines are due. A DP2 student at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC or Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo carrying two sciences at Higher Level will deprioritise her French writing in exactly that fortnight. The practical response is to front-load timed writing into the quieter months of DP1 rather than to schedule more of it into February.

The monsoon removes evening home classes across the city from June to September, and the families who plan a makeup slot at the point of booking lose almost nothing while the families who improvise lose a month. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of the schools named on this page, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, or with any language-certification body.
bullets: The oral recording window is set by your school, not by the IB timetable.
Ask the coordinator for the date in the first term of DP2.
Eight weeks out: unfamiliar images aloud, no notes.
Two weeks out: full conditions with a recording running.
Front-load timed writing into DP1, away from the mock and IA cluster.

sections.heading: Do home classes suit the writing better than online?
paragraphs: For marking, yes, clearly. IB DP French B home tuition in Mumbai lets a tutor sit beside the student with a second pen and annotate a handwritten page while she watches the annotations appear. The student sees where the marker's eye stops. She sees the same correction symbol land three times on one page and understands something that a returned file never conveys. Since Paper 1 is handwritten, practising on paper with a person who marks on paper removes an entire layer of translation.

A home tutor also controls the conditions. A timed task actually gets timed. The phone goes in another room. The student cannot look anything up. That is harder to enforce over a connection, where the tutor has no idea what else is open on the screen. For the oral, being in the room means the tutor can hand over a printed image the student has never seen and start asking questions ten seconds later, which is much closer to the real thing than a shared screen with a loading delay.

What home classes cost you is reach and flexibility. The French B pool is concentrated, so an IB home tutor in Mumbai is far easier to arrange in Khar West than in Panvel, and you are paying for travel time in one currency or another. An IB online tutor in Mumbai solves exactly that, works well for listening and reading, and makes a short midweek session possible when a second house call never would be. The rule for online is simple: writing stays longhand on paper, photographed and marked as an image, because typing hides accents, agreement and the handwriting legibility that a real script depends on.

Most families land on hybrid by the second term: one longer home session for writing and oral rehearsal, one short online session midweek for listening and error drilling. Parents who start by searching "IB tutors near me Mumbai" and expect a map of options usually discover the real constraint is subject scarcity rather than distance. The best IB tutor in Mumbai for your daughter is the one who has marked this course and can reach you every week without heroics. An IB private tutor Mumbai families keep for two years is almost always a local one.
bullets: Home classes: annotation watched live, conditions actually enforced.
A printed unseen image beats a shared screen for oral practice.
Online reaches scarce French B markers and suits listening work.
Online writing stays handwritten, photographed, marked as an image.
Hybrid: one home session weekly plus a short midweek online slot.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with a draft, and what she may never do
paragraphs: This is the boundary, and it should be stated plainly before anybody starts. A tutor may teach a text type, show a model she has written herself as an example, explain why a construction is wrong, mark a draft against the assessment criteria, annotate it, talk the student through every annotation, and mark the revised version afterwards. A tutor may never write, redraft or supply any part of what the student submits. Not a sentence to be copied out, not a corrected paragraph, not a phrase for the oral handed over to be memorised and presented as the student's own work.

The grey area in practice is correction. Marking a draft and saying that the second paragraph loses the formal register is teaching. Writing the second paragraph correctly in the margin so the student can transcribe it is not, even though it feels like help and even though the student will prefer it. The test is whether the words that reach the examiner originated with the student. If a tutor offers to polish a submission before it goes in, that is not a service, and the right response is to end the engagement and tell us.

Before a profile reaches a parent, each IB DP French B home tutor in Mumbai on this platform has had government photo identification verified, the qualification they claim checked, and their French B history examined by component rather than in general terms. References are telephoned. Where a tutor states examining or moderating experience, we ask for specifics. None of this replaces your own checking, which should include asking her to mark a piece of your child's writing in front of you and explain the marks.

Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade. The oral is recorded and moderated, Paper 1 is marked by somebody nobody in the room has met, and no honest teacher claims to know the outcome. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school, the International Baccalaureate organisation or any language-certification body, and we do not guarantee grades. What a good match reliably buys is fewer marks lost to things that are not knowledge, which is a smaller promise and a true one.
bullets: Allowed: teaching, modelling, annotating, marking and re-marking a draft.
Not allowed: supplying sentences, rewriting sections, scripting the oral.
The test is whether the submitted words originated with the student.
Photo ID, qualification and component-level French B history verified.
Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade on a moderated component.

sections.heading: How do you prepare for the individual oral without memorising it?
paragraphs: By rehearsing structures instead of sentences. A memorised oral sounds fluent for ninety seconds and then meets its first follow-up question and stops, because the student has prepared an answer rather than the ability to answer. What survives questioning is a set of reusable moves: a way to open a description, a way to move from what is in the image to what it suggests, a way to concede a point and come back, a way to buy two seconds without switching to English.

Describing a visual stimulus analytically is a trainable skill and most students are never taught it. The weak version lists objects: there is a woman, she is wearing a sari, there are buildings behind. The strong version says what the image is doing. Who is in it and what relationship is implied. Where and when it seems to be set, and what evidence in the image says so. What the photographer chose to include and leave out. What situation it represents in connection with the theme it was chosen for, and whether the student agrees with the view it implies. A tutor should be drilling that order with a different unfamiliar image every week until it becomes automatic.

Then come the follow-up questions, which are where orals are won and lost. The student needs practice being pushed: asked why, then asked why again about her answer, then asked to give an example, then asked whether the opposite might also be true. A home tutor is well placed to do this because she can see when the student is about to give up and keep going anyway. Useful habits include restating the question in French to buy thinking time, saying clearly that she had not considered something and then considering it aloud, and giving a concrete example from her own life in Mumbai rather than a general claim.

Rehearsal that works looks like this: a new image every session, five minutes of unprepared speech, then questions, then two minutes of feedback on language and two on content, then the same image again with the improvements. Record occasionally and make her listen, because students are usually wrong about which bits were weak. What does not work is a written plan she learns, a list of phrases she inserts regardless of relevance, or practising the same three images until she sounds polished on exactly those three. Examiners hear memorisation immediately, and a moderated recording preserves it.
bullets: Rehearse transferable structures, not prepared sentences.
Move from what is in the image to what the image implies.
Name the evidence in the picture for every inference made.
Practise being pushed: why, why again, an example, the counter-case.
A new unfamiliar image every session, then the same one again improved.
Record sometimes; students misjudge which parts were weak.

sections.heading: Building accuracy from your child's own errors, not a grammar book
paragraphs: Generic grammar drilling is the default because it is easy to plan, and it is mostly wasted. A student does not need every tense revised. She needs the four things she personally gets wrong, repeatedly, in every piece she writes. Those four things are discoverable in twenty minutes from two marked scripts and they are specific to her: the agreement she forgets with a preceding direct object, the preposition she picks by English instinct, the adjective she puts in the wrong position, the tu that appears on the third page of every formal piece.

So the tool is an error log, kept on paper in the house, added to from every marked piece, with a tally beside each entry. The entries are written in her own hand with a correct example she produced herself. Five minutes at the start of each session goes to the top three by tally, not to whatever chapter comes next. An error drops off the list when it has not appeared in three consecutive pieces. This is unglamorous and it is the single highest-return thing a home tutor does, because it attacks marks that are being lost for no reason rather than marks that require new learning.

What that produces, in time: at four weeks, the student starts catching her own errors mid-sentence, which is the first sign anything has changed. At one term, the top errors on the original list have been replaced by subtler ones and her written pieces are recognisably in the right text type. Across a full exam cycle, the gain is almost entirely in marks that were being thrown away rather than in a new level of French. That is a real and substantial improvement, and it is also why we do not guarantee grades and why a tutor who offers a number before meeting the student is telling you about herself.

If the arrangement is not working, say so in week three. The signals are specific on this kind of page: no error log has appeared, no timed writing has been done, the tutor talks more than the student, or the oral practice is the same two images every time. We rematch and ask the outgoing tutor for a handover note so the error log survives the change. Replacing a tutor is routine and nobody needs a case built against anybody.
bullets: Two marked scripts reveal the four errors that actually recur.
Keep a paper error log with a tally, in the student's own handwriting.
Five minutes a session on the top three errors by tally.
An error leaves the list after three clean pieces in a row.
No error log and no timed writing by week three means rematch.

sections.heading: Your first French B home tuition session in Mumbai
paragraphs: French B home classes Mumbai families book should start with work, not with a conversation about the course. Have three things ready: two marked pieces of writing with the teacher's comments still on them, the school's theme list, and the date of the individual oral if the coordinator has given one. If the oral date exists, the whole plan is built backwards from it, and if it does not exist yet, chasing it is the most useful thing you can do this month.

In the session itself, expect a timed written task set on the spot, marked in front of your daughter with the criteria named out loud, and an error log started on paper before the tutor leaves. Expect an unfamiliar image produced from a folder and five minutes of unprepared speech about it, followed by questions she did not see coming. If the hour instead goes on explaining the assessment structure to you, you have your answer about the tutor and you have only spent an hour finding out.

Set the physical arrangement up once. A table, good light, the phone in another room, a printer or at least a scanning app on a phone so written work can be sent for marking between sessions. If your building runs a visitor-pass system, put a standing weekly entry on the register with the society office before session one rather than calling the gate every Tuesday evening. Ten minutes of a paid hour lost at the gate each week adds up to a great deal over two years, and one email prevents it.

Then the pattern holds: one longer home session a week, a short online session midweek if the geography demands it, a file of marked writing you can open at any point, an error log that shortens, and a review at four weeks where you and the tutor say out loud what has changed. Whatever IB tuition fees in Mumbai come to for your match, that review is where you decide whether it is worth continuing, and a good tutor will expect to be asked.
bullets: Bring two marked pieces, the theme list and the oral date.
Expect a timed task marked in front of the student in session one.
Expect one unfamiliar image and five minutes of unprepared speech.
Arrange a standing society gate pass before the first visit.
Book the four-week review at the same time as the first session.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP French B home tutor in Mumbai do about the Paper 1 writing task?
faqs.answer: She sets it, times it, and marks it where your child can see the marking happen. A good IB DP French B home tutor in Mumbai works on the task brief before the writing starts, making the student identify the audience, the purpose and the named text type and annotate them in the margin. Then a timed piece by hand, then annotation against the criteria with each symbol explained aloud, then a rewrite of the weakest section rather than the whole thing. Over a term that cycle repeats across different text types until the conventions stop requiring conscious thought.

faqs.question: What text types could come up in the writing task?
faqs.answer: The course works across a range of them, and the usual suspects are a formal letter, an email, a blog post, an article, a speech, a report, a set of instructions, a diary entry, a brochure or leaflet, an interview and a review. Your school's teacher will be working from the current subject guide, so ask which list the class is using. The practical point is that each one has openings, closings, a person, a register and a layout of its own, and a student who has practised four of them and met a fifth in the exam is improvising conventions she could have learned in twenty minutes.

faqs.question: How do you practise the individual oral without writing a script?
faqs.answer: By practising with material she has never seen. A new unfamiliar image every session, five minutes of unprepared speech, then follow-up questions, then feedback split between language and content, then the same image again done better. What gets rehearsed is structure: how to open a description, how to move from what is shown to what it implies, how to concede and recover, how to buy two seconds in French. Phrases learned by heart and inserted regardless of relevance are audible to an examiner, and the oral is recorded and moderated, so a memorised performance does not pass unnoticed.

faqs.question: My daughter freezes when the examiner asks a follow-up question. What helps?
faqs.answer: Practice at being pushed, deliberately and often. Most students have only ever answered one question per topic, so the second one feels like an attack. The fix is a tutor who asks why, then asks why about the answer, then asks for an example, then asks whether the opposite might be true, every session. Useful habits: restating the question in French to buy thinking time, saying plainly that she had not thought about it and then thinking aloud, and reaching for a concrete example from her own life in Mumbai instead of a general statement. Freezing is a trained-out problem, not a personality trait.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor come to our flat in Kharghar on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes if the tutor is based in Navi Mumbai, and we will tell you honestly if that pool is thin for French B. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur and Panvel are all a short drive from Kharghar along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway. A tutor crossing from Juhu or Bandra over the Atal Setu for a seven o'clock weekday slot will manage it for a few weeks and then start rescheduling, which is worse for the student than a different arrangement would have been. For outer nodes a Saturday morning home session plus a short midweek online slot usually holds for two years.

faqs.question: Where in the home should the session actually happen?
faqs.answer: At a table, in a room with a door that stays open, with the student's phone somewhere else. The dining table is usually better than a study, because a study has a computer in it. You need good light for marking handwritten work and somewhere to spread two papers side by side. Avoid a bedroom. For the oral practice part, a wall without clutter behind the student helps if anything is being recorded. None of this is fussiness: a timed written task done on a sofa with a phone face-down nearby is not a timed written task.

faqs.question: Is the individual oral really marked by her own teacher?
faqs.answer: It is conducted and assessed internally by the school and then moderated externally, which is a meaningful difference from Paper 1. In practice that means the person asking the questions knows your daughter, the recording is reviewed by somebody who does not, and the school's marking can be adjusted. Two consequences follow. First, the date is set by the school, so you can plan backwards from it, which you cannot do with an externally timetabled paper. Second, a performance that sounds memorised is preserved on the recording for the moderator, so rehearsal has to produce fluency rather than recitation.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for French B home tuition?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length. French B is scarce in this city, because the number of teachers who have planned its themes and marked its written tasks is much smaller than the number who teach French, and scarcity moves a rate more than difficulty does. Higher Level costs more than Standard Level. Travel is a real input for home visits: a tutor driving from Khar West to Kharghar is pricing the road as well as the hour. We will not print a figure here, because any number on a page would be wrong for somebody reading it.

faqs.question: Can the tutor correct her draft before she hands it in?
faqs.answer: She can mark it and she cannot rewrite it. Marking means annotating against the criteria, naming the problems, explaining them aloud and marking the revised version afterwards. Rewriting means supplying corrected sentences in the margin for your daughter to copy out, and that crosses the line however helpful it feels at the time. The test is whether the words the examiner reads originated with the student. If a tutor offers to clean a piece up before submission, end the engagement and tell us, because that offer puts the student's whole Diploma at risk rather than just one task.

faqs.question: She knows the grammar rules but keeps making the same mistakes. Why?
faqs.answer: Because knowing a rule and applying it under time pressure are different skills, and generic grammar revision trains only the first. The fix is specific rather than broad: pull her four personal recurring errors out of two marked scripts, write them in an error log in her own handwriting with a correct example she produced, and spend five minutes at the start of each session on the top three by tally. An error leaves the list after three clean pieces in a row. This is far more productive than working through a grammar book she can already recite.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor's commute makes her late on Ghodbunder Road?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens rather than during it. The usual arrangement is that the session still runs for its full length where the household can absorb a later finish, or the missing minutes are added to the next one, and a cancellation with reasonable notice is rescheduled rather than charged. Ghodbunder Road between Majiwada and Kasarvadavali is the most reliable source of this problem in Thane, as the Western Express Highway is in the suburbs. Where a slot keeps slipping, the honest answer is usually a different time or a local tutor, not more apologies.

faqs.question: Does she need different tutors for the oral and the writing?
faqs.answer: No, and splitting them is usually counterproductive. The same errors show up in both, the error log serves both, and the analytical habits built for describing an image feed directly into the opinion sections of written tasks. One tutor who does both sees the whole picture and can shift the weekly balance as the oral date approaches and then back again afterwards. Where a split occasionally makes sense is at Higher Level, if the literary works are genuinely outside a tutor's experience, and in that case we would rather tell you than pretend otherwise.
